stories.Headline: How Founders Select Top Experts for AI Transformation: Avoid Treating Tool-Only Users as Core Leaders
stories.Summary:
Founders undergoing AI transformation often make a hiring mistake: they hand operational problems to an AI-savvy hire and expect that person to solve everything alone. An article published by 36Kr on 13 November 2026 used an example from a private gathering in Hangzhou on 23 October, where an AI transformation expert named IS described an e-commerce owner who hired a skilled IT specialist. Every time that specialist tried to schedule a meeting with business leads, they ignored him. When asked what AI meant to the company, the owner said it was a matter of survival, and IS pointed out that the survival task had been given to someone on the job for only two months. The article argues that many founders, including those with annual revenue of hundreds of millions to over a billion yuan, fail to set priorities or define responsibilities.

Another AI transformation expert, XD, described a project that started before the 618 shopping festival, when the company needed more advertising creatives. The existing shooting and editing team had limited capacity and inconsistent quality, and expanding it would have required more hires and spending. XD's team included himself as operation lead, internal and external content experts, and a dedicated AI junior specialist. Their workflow covered analysing data, grading creatives, and generating scripts and storyboards. After a week or two, the process still failed because no one oversaw the links between steps, such as whether the AI understood the product and its differences from competitors.

XD personally re-ran the workflow, breaking each step into human inputs, AI outputs, and the standards results had to meet before moving on. Creatives meant to build product awareness were judged differently from those meant to drive conversions, and humans decided which metrics applied. Hard-to-edit materials were assigned to humans and easy-to-edit ones to AI. One night at about 11 PM, XD told the execution team group that he had worked out the full feasible workflow. During the 618 festival, the workflow reportedly raised advertising ROI by about 25 percent and increased creative supply by about 30 percent without additional headcount.

XD also granted performance exemptions during the trial period and prepared incentives in advance. Creatives that underperformed in ad delivery were not penalised under the old assessment rules, while good results were to be rewarded. The article notes that many business owners overlook this, since employees exploring new workflows must carve time from existing work while old performance indicators still apply. A founder asked XD whether the boss must personally validate workflows, and XD answered that consultants with on-ground implementation capability can run one or two projects first, but the founder must set overall strategy, select the first task, allocate resources, and resolve cross-departmental conflicts. The article states that organisational problems are often mistaken for a lack of talent, and that companies need different talent at different stages.

The article's authors, identified only as the contributor 张美吉 and the 36Kr platform, state that the views belong to the author and that 36Kr provides only information storage services. They recommend pairing people with rich business experience, who make judgments, with fast learners and strong doers, who deliver results, rather than loading every requirement into one "AI lead" role. They also suggest that companies with annual revenue between 100 million and 3 billion yuan reassess their teams to identify who can set standards, run workflows, and lead the original team. The article says such hires should be measured by whether they have delivered tangible results and whether their methods can become capabilities the company keeps. The article does not report any response from the e-commerce owner, and it gives no further details on how the new roles would be structured or how their results would be measured over time.

Articles.Title: How Founders Select Top Experts for AI Transformation: Avoid Treating Tool-Only Users as Core Leaders - 36Kr

stories.Headline: 50,000 Yuan Graphics Card Trend: Is AI Pushing Gamers Out of the PC Hardware Market?
stories.Summary:
In late October, high-end Nvidia RTX 50 series graphics cards in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei market saw 11 consecutive trading days of price increases, according to a 36kr report published on 13 November 2026. The RTX 5080 quote on e-commerce platforms once approached 20,000 yuan, while the Huaqiangbei channel quote for the RTX 5090 reached 51,000 to 55,000 yuan. Some merchants even offered higher prices than that range during the rally. A gaming graphics card that originally sold for over 10,000 yuan was now quoted at more than 50,000 yuan. The report described the episode as a rare price roller coaster ride in the Shenzhen hardware market.

The RTX 5090's initial official retail price was about 15,000 to 16,000 yuan, and the RTX 5080's initial selling price was about 8,000 yuan. Starting from 28 October, prices suddenly reversed downward, and the RTX 5080 fell back from nearly 20,000 yuan to 16,000 yuan. Some models saw obvious single-day declines, and by early November Huaqiangbei merchants had begun to stock goods cautiously. The RTX 5090 is equipped with 32GB of video memory, which the report said has certain advantages in local AI applications. Nvidia executives publicly denied a production suspension of the RTX 5090 and said the product will continue to be shipped.

The report said Nvidia admitted there are certain constraints on supply chain production capacity. It said Nvidia operates both consumer-grade GPU and data center computing businesses, and the data center business has become its most important source of revenue as AI infrastructure investment grows. The report said the weight of consumer-grade gaming graphics cards in the company's overall business is significantly lower. It said Nvidia certainly has more incentive to prioritize securing the high-profit, high-demand AI computing market. It also said Nvidia cannot arbitrarily shift all gaming graphics card production capacity to AI chips, because the two product types differ in chip design, packaging, video memory configuration and supply chain links.

A Shenzhen server parts wholesaler previously interviewed by Jiemian News said the October price increase was due not only to tight production capacity but also to news stimulation and channel speculation, according to the report. The report said downstream PC manufacturers and consumers may not be willing to take orders when prices rise too high, and channel inventory may turn into pressure. It said gamers are the most directly affected group, with those who planned to spend about 8,000 yuan to upgrade now possibly needing more than 10,000 yuan. The report said some people choose to postpone the upgrade, some turn to previous-generation products, and some simply give up high-end discrete graphics cards. It said graphics card manufacturers face rising chip and video memory costs, channel merchants bear price fluctuations and inventory risks, and complete machine manufacturers need to recalculate product costs.

The report said the price fluctuation was on the surface driven jointly by production suspension rumors, tight supply and channel speculation. It said that in the past graphics cards were mainly sold to gamers, but now AI developers, small and medium-sized enterprises and studios have also begun to compete for this type of hardware. It said more and more developers are trying to run large models locally, and design studios can use high-end cards to run tools like ComfyUI and Stable Diffusion. It said demand from AI servers for HBM high-bandwidth memory continues to grow, and memory manufacturers are shifting resources to higher-margin products, which may affect the supply and cost of consumer-grade video memory such as GDDR6 and GDDR7. It said consumer-grade graphics cards cannot completely replace professional AI computing cards, and large-scale model training and enterprise-level computing still require professional products.

The report said that when the price of an RTX 5090 reaches tens of thousands of yuan, the cost gap between purchasing hardware and renting cloud computing power needs to be recalculated. It said that if hardware prices are too high, on-demand rental of computing power may be more cost-effective. It said what really determines graphics card prices in the longer term is whether supply can recover, whether AI demand can be sustained, and whether consumers are willing to pay high prices. It said the episode leaves a clear signal that graphics cards are no longer just equipment for gamers but also a computing resource in the AI era. It said gamers used to determine how much a graphics card was worth, and now AI developers, data centers and upstream supply chains have also begun to participate in pricing.

Articles.Title: 50,000 Yuan Graphics Card Trend: Is AI Pushing Gamers Out of the PC Hardware Market? - 36Kr

stories.Headline: AI Comic Drama Boom: Why Ordinary People Get-Rich-Quick Dreams Can’t Ride the Trend
stories.Summary:
The articles report that a boom in AI comic dramas has not delivered get-rich-quick results for ordinary people, and that training and franchise offers are proliferating, as published by eu.36kr.com on 2026-11-12T06:00:00Z under the byline 文娱先声. DataEye Research Institute data show that in the first half of this year 221,900 new AI dramas and manhua dramas launched on Douyin, and only 1055 works passed 100 million views, about 0.48%. Using DataEye's 50 million views as the break-even line, only 2886 works reached that scale, about 1.3%. A person in charge of an AI manhua drama company told China Newsweek that revenue per 10,000 views for a work over 100 million views once exceeded 100 yuan but by May this year had fallen to 30 to 50 yuan. Creator Xingyu Shinyo said her 12-episode work I Become the Most Eloquent Spokesperson for My Father the Emperor cost 1715 yuan to make and earned 19.64 yuan.

The articles say the work's popularity value reached 14.85 million a month after launch, actual views exceeded 49,000, and revenue per 10,000 views was only 3.97 yuan. Economist Fu Peng of Xinhuo Group said almost all AI manhua dramas lost money in the past three months, and he estimated that self-bought traffic promotion accounts for about 80% to 90% of total cost, computing power about 10%, and hardware depreciation leaves only about 5% profit. On the Changdu distribution platform under Fanqie, the articles say, creators deliver a finished film after obtaining IP authorization while distributors select products, pay for traffic and share revenue by conversion. Hongguo's "Guoran Plan" rates projects by script outline, character setting, planning document and Demo, and its policy announced on November 12 sets a 15,000 yuan minimum guarantee for S-level AI scripts, no minimum for A-level, and no cooperation for B-level. Creator Xiaoguogege of The Little Carpenter from Anhui told media practitioner Pan Luan that his low-end drama earned 1.5 yuan per 10,000 views against 12 yuan for high-quality dramas, an 8-fold gap.

Fu Peng called creators "digital tenant farmers" working for platforms, saying AI raised content production efficiency but did not change platform bidding distribution and benefit distribution, so saved production cost is swallowed by traffic buying. Xiaoguogege advised people with shooting, editing, self-media or novel promotion experience to try on a small scale and people with no relevant experience not to participate blindly. Zhang Hansheng, chief planner of Travel to Song Dynasty with Weapons, said AI equality only means equal access to the model and the creation threshold has not disappeared, with content and creative ideas still key. Zhang said "AI itself has no emotions" and feelings of family and country, emotions and moods must be endowed by creators, and he warned against packaging AI manhua dramas as easy money from a training course. The articles say training institutions advertise 9.9-yuan introductory courses up to courses costing thousands or tens of thousands of yuan, promising zero-foundation learning, mastery in three days and orders within a week.

The articles report that a consumer in Hubei was charged 59,800 yuan by a network company in Jinan for a "regional agent" AI manhua drama production system, promised operation learned in half an hour and revenue from developing lower-level agents, but found the system was public internet resources and the exclusive regional right could not be fulfilled. The articles say some intermediaries recruit creators under banners of platform orders, minimum guaranteed revenue and internal resources, then charge computing power fees or deposits or pass production costs and rework risks to individuals through multi-layer subcontracting. The articles say Soochow University junior Xiao Tianle earned more than 3 million yuan in revenue from AI manhua dramas, a trending topic, and his team produced hundreds of manhua dramas in under a year with only one real hit, also taking commercial orders so income was not purely platform revenue sharing. The articles say mastering basic AI tool operation differs from producing works independently, since image generation, video generation, script adaptation and shot design require long practice and repeated trial and error. The articles say many people who buy AI courses end up paying for a useless "stupidity tax".

The articles say the AI manhua drama market is hot but that does not mean people can make money lying down or that everyone can share the profits. The articles say playback revenue of AI manhua dramas has declined rapidly since the beginning of this year, and half a year on the situation is even more unpromising. The articles say high-quality dramas with more refined scene polishing and higher production investment can get several times or even more revenue per 10,000 views than ordinary low-end works. The articles say the high traffic investment cost Fu Peng described mainly fits business models where creators bear traffic-buying costs themselves and does not fully apply to platforms such as Fanqie. The articles say whether a work obtains platform resources, how much traffic it gets after launch and how much revenue it shares are still affected by content quality, platform project screening, traffic distribution and revenue sharing rules.

The articles say AI tools lower the entry threshold but do not make making money easier, and ordinary people still have a long way to go from work competition to traffic acquisition to content creation before getting real returns from the track. The articles say the copyright investment model opens high-quality IP only to a few head contractors. The articles say the "free pie falling from the sky" that ordinary people see is never that simple in reality. The articles say the success stories of hundreds of millions of views, over one million yuan in revenue and financial freedom in a few months circulate alongside growing advertisements for AI manhua drama training and franchise. The articles say institutions signal to ordinary people that now is the perfect time to enter the field, from zero-based entry to quick order receiving and from low-cost entrepreneurship to stable returns.

The articles do not say what happens next for the market, the platforms or the training and franchise institutions. The articles leave open who exactly is luring ordinary people into the trap, beyond naming training institutions, investment promotion and system service providers, and MCN institutions and project intermediaries. The articles leave open how the revenue decline will develop now that half a year has passed since May. The articles leave open how platform screening, traffic distribution and revenue sharing rules will change. The articles leave open whether ordinary people with relevant experience who try on a small scale will recover their costs.

stories.Headline: WorkBuddy & Codex Drive AI Competition to Task-Centric Delivery: Reliability as the Non-Negotiable Hard Threshold
stories.Summary:
WorkBuddy and Codex are pushing AI competition toward task delivery, where reliability has become a hard threshold, according to an article published by 36Kr on November 12, 2026. The piece, drawn from a WeChat article by the Yiou Think Tank with author Zhu Luman, argues that the evaluation unit of AI office work is turning into a task that can be checked and accepted on completion. It contrasts asking an AI to explain how to make a business analysis with asking it to read sales tables, calculate metrics, generate charts and deliver a report. The article says users now judge products by whether the task is completed, not only by whether the answer is excellent.

The article describes WorkBuddy as a product that treats local file operations, autonomous planning and result delivery as core capabilities. In an official practice example for business analysis, users supply an Excel or CSV file, specify metrics and time ranges, and the product reads the data, performs statistics and generates charts or reports. Codex, first released in 2025, handled code reading, command execution and test runs, and in June 2026 OpenAI disclosed that knowledge work such as reports, spreadsheets, presentations and research analysis had been added. In August, OpenAI opened Codex's execution loop as an integrable Harness that other applications can use.

The article attributes these developments to product teams and their platforms rather than to a single new model. Tencent's WorkBuddy page and OpenAI's Codex materials are cited as the sources describing these capabilities. The article argues that a "domain expert" label on a task does not by itself show an independently trained vertical model, since professional capability can come from general models, task descriptions, materials, tools and execution control working together. Its authors present model specialization as only one of several implementation methods.

The article reports that general models have grown better at following instructions, handling long documents and calling tools, which reduces the need for separate processing logic per task. It traces the technical context to 2018 early GPT research on pre-training followed by fine-tuning, to GPT-3 in 2020 completing tasks from in-context descriptions and examples, to 2020 RAG research adding external retrieval, and to a 2024 Berkeley BAIR summary of "composite AI systems." It notes that RAG, fine-tuning, workflows and agents developed in overlapping periods rather than replacing one another. The article also says that Dify added a Human Input node in March 2026 and that Salesforce's Agentforce documentation separates deterministic logic from model reasoning.

Those affected include enterprise users whose contracts, inventories and business records change daily and cannot wait for retraining, and developers choosing between retrieval, training and workflow design. The article states that the choice between retrieval and training depends on whether a shortfall comes from missing information or from unstable task performance. It adds that long tasks lasting dozens of minutes, with file changes and tool failures, need systems that track completed steps and resume after errors. Anthropic's engineering practice for long-running tasks, using progress files and version records, is cited as one approach.

The article points to research on reliable agents, including Nature's Paper2Agent and Science's Biomni, which it says focus on runnable, verifiable systems. It also cites a 2026 ICML study of 15 models that found recent capability gains produce only small reliability improvements. The article concludes that a single accuracy figure cannot capture repeated runs, input changes and failure consequences, and that task quality, repeated-run performance, manual review and total cost should be observed together. The articles do not say what specific products will ship next or how competitors will respond.

Articles.Title: WorkBuddy & Codex Drive AI Competition to Task-Centric Delivery: Reliability as the Non-Negotiable Hard Threshold - 36Kr

stories.Headline: AI Pinpoints Pathogenic Cells from DNA – Google AlphaGenome 2 Unlocks New Drug Targets for Diabetes and Cancer
stories.Summary:
Google DeepMind has released AlphaGenome 2, a new-generation model that predicts how DNA mutations act in specific cell types and which genes they affect. The model is presented as a way to trace the root causes of diseases and find more accurate drug targets for conditions such as cancer and diabetes. The announcement was reported by 36Kr on November 12, 2026, with the Chinese outlet QbitAI listed as the original source. The model was trained on data from 68 types of tissue and more than 107 million cells, covering both human and mouse cells. In a test covering 28 types of immune cells, its recall rate for identifying key causal variants reached 30 percent, compared with 16 percent for the previous generation after fine-tuning with single-cell data.

Its ability to judge whether a variant strengthens or weakens gene activity rose from 23 percent to 43 percent. The article says the model can adapt to new single-cell data without retraining and can predict DNA methylation. Google CEO Sundar Pichai framed the work around the idea that cells share the same DNA blueprint but read it differently, so a variant may matter only in one cell type. The article also quotes Sarah Teichmann, a professor at the University of Cambridge and co-founder of the Human Cell Atlas Consortium, who praised the model's ability to work with small numbers of cell samples.

The piece presents these statements as enthusiasm about the tool rather than as independent validation of its clinical value. In one example, the article says James Lee's team spent a year and a half of experiments to link a DNA variant in a "gene desert" to over-activation of the ETS2 gene in intestinal immune cells, linked to inflammatory bowel disease. According to the article, AlphaGenome 2 reproduced the key finding through calculation in about half an hour. The model is available for non-commercial research through an API and an interactive Colab tutorial, and Google plans to add it to its Agent toolbox and to Google Antigravity as AlphaGenome 2 Skills.

Articles.Title: AI Pinpoints Pathogenic Cells from DNA – Google AlphaGenome 2 Unlocks New Drug Targets for Diabetes and Cancer - 36Kr

stories.Headline: AI Computing Power Rent-Collecting Business: Undergoing a Transformative Sea Change
stories.Summary:
Zhou Yong, a computing power landlord with tens of billions of yuan in orders, began reaching out to key clients after the end of the second quarter of this year to strike a rarely seen deal. He replaced a long-standing fixed cabinet rental fee for GPU computing power with a revenue-sharing scheme tied to the call volume of AI Tokens. Economic Observer reporters interviewed several upstream and downstream enterprises in the computing power industry chain and found that many service providers had adopted similar practices. Some providers cut the fixed service fee by about 10% in contracts while raising the Token revenue share by more than 200%. Public information showed that during this year's "Double 11" promotion, top live streamers sold nearly 100,000 large model Token monthly cards in half an hour.

Under the new model, the guaranteed minimum fee is cut, and the excess Token output above an agreed threshold is divided according to an agreed proportion. In one example, a customer's annual rigid computing power spending of about 120 million yuan falls to 108 million yuan. Zhou Yong's company calculated that if the customer's inference call volume rises steadily, its annual comprehensive income could rise by 20% to 50% over the original fixed rent scheme. If call volume stays below baseline for a long time, however, its annual revenue could drop by up to 10%. The arrangement has been piloted since the first quarter of 2026 between leading domestic providers and large model and Agent application makers, and it has not yet reached small and medium-sized customers or training orders.

Zhou Yong said the change amounts to a reconstruction of the internal revenue structure of long-term orders, in which the provider gives up part of its fixed return in exchange for a share of the downstream inference growth. Wang Daowei, head of Token business at a listed South China provider, said his company now includes share clauses in new contracts. One project type uses MaaS joint operation profit sharing, with the provider supplying computing infrastructure and the model maker supplying model capability, while another type sells Tokens directly with an annual guaranteed minimum plus pay-as-you-go billing for overseas orders. Wang Daowei added that more than one peer is running similar pilots, though their degree of disclosure varies. Customers gain lower upfront rigid costs, while providers gain a deeper binding to the customer's business.

Customers are shifting toward enterprise Agents and industry large models, whose call volumes are growing quickly, while general casual chat grows more gently. A procurement head at a leading cloud vendor said this demand shift is pushing customers to reduce upfront fixed costs and pushing providers to share the benefits of inference growth. The person in charge of computing power at a leading large model company said his firm runs a hybrid architecture, with its own cluster handling stable core work and external computing power for elastic expansion. A business person at a leading domestic AI chip maker said assessment now focuses on how many Tokens each hardware unit actually outputs and the cost of a single Token. A bank financing manager said such projects carry notably higher risk than ordinary manufacturing, so banks raise risk premiums and demand combined credit enhancement.

The articles leave open how widely the sharing model will spread, since Wang Daowei said it is not yet at a comprehensive inflection point and predicted traditional long-term rental will still dominate ordinary customers and training businesses. They also leave open whether hardware output will meet expectations, because the chip iteration cycle runs about 1.5 to 2 years while accounting depreciation may reach 3 to 4 years and commercial life is often shorter. Zhou Yong said shared revenue depends on the delivery and acceptance of computing power units and customer activity, and that risk is shared in both directions. The bank said its first repayment source is downstream real business cash flow, though the articles do not say how banks will weigh these factors in practice.

Articles.Title: AI Computing Power Rent-Collecting Business: Undergoing a Transformative Sea Change - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Absurd "Made in India" AI Model Exposed as Repackaged Qwen3.5: Huge Fiasco Uncovered, Even Forcing AI to Claim "Originates from India"
stories.Summary:
The Indian AI company 169Pi released Alpie Seed 9B on November 8, a multimodal reasoning model with 9 billion parameters. It accepts text, image and video input, supports a 262K context window, and was promoted as able to run offline on workstations, laptops and smartphones. The company presented it as a new achievement for India's AI research field, timing the promotion around the Diwali festival. Shortly after release, developers examined the configuration files and found that the model's base was Alibaba's Qwen3.5-9B.

The model's architecture, tokenizer vocabulary and weight structure were found to be highly consistent with Qwen3.5-9B. The team reported using supervised fine-tuning with DoRA, adjusting parameters such as the attention layers and feedforward networks. A second stage used GRPO reinforcement learning across seven reward dimensions, including answer correctness, hallucination penalty and answer length. That stage ran on 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs for 3,034 training steps, consuming about 3,472 GPU hours. The Chat Template also contained an identity_policy instruction telling the model to say it was developed by 169Pi and came from India.

Developers who criticized the project argued that the identity prompt was a deliberate attempt to present the model as Indian-built. Netizens on X, including a user identified as "Dongxi NLP," said the model was effectively a tribute to Qwen3.5-9B. Some commenters said open-source fine-tuning was acceptable but that the original authors' work should be acknowledged. Others argued public criticism was too harsh, since many startups fine-tune open models and such post-training work has its own value. The debate centered on whether the project can fairly be called independently developed Indian technology.

Independent developer Satyajit published a technical analysis on November 9 comparing the Safetensors files of both models. He sampled and compared all 760 tensors and ran full hash verification and value-by-value decoding on some of them. His results showed that Alpie Seed retains the original Qwen3.5-9B architecture, and that parts such as the visual encoder and word embedding layer remain unchanged. The changes were concentrated in some attention layers and feedforward networks, so the parameter share actually altered was not high. His article concluded the model is a post-trained derivative, not a foundation model trained from scratch in India.

On November 9, 169Pi issued a statement admitting that Alpie Seed was developed from Qwen3.5-9B and not pre-trained from scratch by its team. The company acknowledged the contributions of the Qwen team and the open-source community, and said it had not sufficiently highlighted the model's origin in earlier promotion. It said its work focused on post-training and engineering optimization, and that running a multimodal 9B model on CPUs, laptops and phones required substantial engineering. 169Pi said it would clearly mark the technical origin in future introductions and was exploring developing its own foundation model. The model is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

Whether the company will change the identity_policy prompt or remove the India-origin claims from the model was not reported in the articles. The articles also do not say whether 169Pi plans to build its own foundation model or when that might happen. How much the post-training work improved Alpie Seed's benchmark results over Qwen3.5-9B is not addressed. The articles do not report any formal response from Alibaba or the Qwen team. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Absurd "Made in India" AI Model Exposed as Repackaged Qwen3.5: Huge Fiasco Uncovered, Even Forcing AI to Claim "Originates from India" - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Google Unveils Gemini Decision 1: Its First-Ever Decision-Making AI Model That Tops 7 Out of 9 Benchmarks With Up to 92.2% Accuracy
stories.Summary:
Google has released Gemini Decision 1, which it describes as its first dedicated decision-making model, together with the Gemini Decisions API that is powered by it. The release was announced on 2026-11-12 in coverage from 36Kr, and Google's own blog post is dated 2026-11-11. Unlike a conventional generative language model, it does not write answers token by token, and instead scores a set of candidate answers supplied in advance in a single forward pass. Google says the model took first place in 7 of 9 benchmark tests, reaching a top accuracy of 92.2%. The API is available in Google AI Studio, and Google's own teams have already started to use the technology.

Developers supply the input, the questions to be judged and the candidate options, and the model returns a judgment, a probability and a confidence level between 0 and 1. It handles three kinds of decisions: yes or no judgments, multiple choice with 2 to 255 options, and ordered rubric scoring that returns a weighted score and the probability of each level. Up to 1000 independent questions can be sent in one request, in text, image, audio, video or PDF form, with a multimodal context of up to 256K tokens. The three task types can be mixed in a single request, such as asking whether a pantry countertop photo shows a spill, what cleaning is needed and how severe the scene is. Pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens with no charge for output tokens, and end-to-end latency is about 150 to 250 milliseconds.

Google is the party responsible, and Chief Executive Sundar Pichai announced the launch in a post on X. He said the API is now live in Google AI Studio and that the model is built for decision tasks within a closed set of options rather than for generating text. He highlighted the three decision types, the low price, which he put at about one-fifth of the cost of Flash-Lite, and its leading results on several benchmarks with the lowest calibration error. Google's technical material adds that the median latency of the model calculation phase stays between 50 and 100 milliseconds in contexts of up to 16K tokens. Google also says latency stays basically stable when a request grows from 1 question to 100.

Google compared the model against three rivals: OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna, TypeSafe Jev 1.14, which is dedicated to classification and decision-making, and its own Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite. On JevBench, Gemini Decision 1 scored 92.2%, ahead of 90.9% for GPT-6 Luna, 90.0% for TypeSafe Jev 1.14 and 86.6% for Flash-Lite. On the New Yorker Caption test it scored 79.7% against 68.4% for GPT-6 Luna, and on PubMedQA it scored 79.8% against 74.4%. TypeSafe Jev 1.14 led two tests: Mind2Web Multimodal, at 86.8% to Gemini's 86.2%, and When2Call, at 82.0% to Gemini's 79.9%. Developers who build agents are the most affected, since tool selection is a key scenario for the model, and the article says competitors also still perform better on total invocation cost in some cases.

Before this, developers who wanted an AI to judge whether an email was spam, or to pick which agent should receive a task, usually called a generative model and extracted the result from its text. Gemini Decision 1 removes the step of decoding word by word. Google says the API costs nearly 5 times less than calling Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite through the Interactions API on the common benchmark set it used. On other benchmarks, Gemini Decision 1 scored 58.7% Macro-F1 on Amazon ESCI product search relevance, 86.0% on Global-MMLU-Lite against 79.6% for GPT-6 Luna, and 71.8% on MMAU and 69.1% on Video-MME, both above Flash-Lite. Its Top-1 expected calibration error is 0.0250, against 0.0721 for GPT-6 Luna, 0.0494 for TypeSafe Jev 1.14 and 0.2104 for Flash-Lite.

Google has described several uses inside its own products. Gemini Notebook uses the Decisions API as a real-time router that picks a model tier and reasoning intensity based on how complex each request is, which Google says can cut latency on daily queries by up to 40%. In Google Stitch, the experimental Rapid Canvas feature uses it to generate interactive product flow wireframes in seconds and to respond to changes made by voice or click. In the CC product from Google Labs, it picks emoji reactions from more than 200 options, and inside Google Search it forms a safety detection layer for MCP tools that looks for adversarial behavior and content. The articles do not say when the model will reach more developers, what pricing will apply after launch, or how it performs outside Google's own comparison.

Articles.Title: Google Unveils Its First Decision-Making AI Model: 1M Tokens Priced As Low As $0.1 With 100% Free Full Output Access - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Can Nvidia’s Self-Developed Protégé Become the Savior of AI Trading?
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave released its third-quarter 2026 financial report after U.S. market hours on November 10 Eastern Time, reporting revenue of 3.66 billion U.S. dollars, a year-on-year increase of 168%, and raised its full-year revenue guidance. The company is a U.S. computing power rental company that has received multiple investments from NVIDIA and is known in the market as "NVIDIA's favorite child". Its share price had fallen by more than 40% in the month before the report was released, one of the hardest hit in the recent stock market decline. After the report, global AI computing power stocks rebounded on November 11. CoreWeave's share price once rose by about 20% during intraday trading after U.S. stocks opened that night.

In the third quarter of 2026, CoreWeave's revenue increased by more than 1 billion U.S. dollars compared with the previous quarter, higher than the upper limit of guidance, and adjusted operating profit was 379 million U.S. dollars against a previous guidance range of 200 million to 260 million U.S. dollars. It raised its full-year revenue guidance to 13 billion to 13.3 billion U.S. dollars. As of the end of September 2026, its on-hand orders were about 132.5 billion U.S. dollars, a year-on-year increase of 138%, and its contracted power capacity exceeded 4.6 gigawatts, of which more than 1.7 gigawatts were put into operation. As of the end of September 2026, its debt size was close to 47 billion U.S. dollars, and interest expense in the third quarter alone reached 846 million U.S. dollars. In January 2026, NVIDIA made an additional investment of 2 billion U.S. dollars in CoreWeave at 87.20 U.S. dollars per share, and as of the close on November 10, CoreWeave's share price was 48.73 U.S. dollars.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said on the financial report conference call that the growth of computing power demand is faster than the ability to deliver these infrastructures. He said the effective demand received by CoreWeave is equivalent to 10 times the production capacity it can provide before the end of 2027, and its production capacity up to 2027 has been almost sold out. He said 10% of Fortune 500 companies in the U.S. are already CoreWeave's customers, and more than half of the new customers added in 2026 come from industries outside the AI and technology sectors. He said CoreWeave raised the prices of all types of products by 25% in July 2026 and by another 10% in the late third quarter, with prices still rising in the fourth quarter. He said more than 130,000 GPUs of CoreWeave will expire under their contracts in 2027, and renewal alone can bring an annualized revenue increment of nearly 4 billion U.S. dollars without additional capital expenditure.

Intrator said the computing power rental prices of the Ampere and Hopper GPUs, released in 2020 and 2022 respectively, rose by 30% to 50% month-on-month at CoreWeave in the third quarter of 2026. He said at the current yield level CoreWeave will not raise funds through the unsecured bond market and there is no need to do so. CoreWeave stated in its financial report that it expects to receive about 9 billion U.S. dollars in customer prepayments and deposits in the next three months. CoreWeave CFO Nitin Agrawal said the next loan linked to customer contracts is expected to have a financing cost of 7% to 7.5%, and that cash flow from existing customer contracts is sufficient to repay the corresponding debt. He said that if only already signed orders are delivered, CoreWeave's capital expenditure in 2027 will be the same as in 2026, while revenue will increase significantly, and adjusted net profit is expected to turn positive in the first half.

A communications industry analyst at a large brokerage firm in South China told the Economic Observer reporter that the report beat the expectations of all institutions and everyone, with revenue and profit both better than market expectations. On November 11, A-share companies Zhongji Xuchuang and Eoptolink rose by 15.07% and 16.97% respectively, both posting their largest single-day gains of the year. Optical device manufacturer TFC rose by 13.96%, and optical chip manufacturer Source Photonics hit the 10% daily price limit. The South Korean and Chinese Taiwan stock markets rose by 2.6% and 3.6% respectively.

In early November, the yield of some CoreWeave bonds once rose to more than 16%, indicating creditors had doubts about its solvency. In early October, public information showed that annualized revenue data OpenAI provided to investors was close to 50 billion U.S. dollars, lower than the previous market expectation of nearly 70 billion U.S. dollars. In late October, U.S. tech giants released their financial reports, and the free cash flow of Amazon, Alphabet and Meta in the third quarter of 2026 was all negative, and Alphabet's share price fell by more than 12% on October 29. The Nasdaq Index fell 5.3% in October and dropped another 5.52% in a single day on November 5, its largest single-day decline since April 2025.

On November 3, the U.S. midterm elections ended, and the Democratic Party won control of the Senate and the House of Representatives. According to UBS estimates, about 30% of the new data center capacity expected to be added in the U.S. by 2028 may be affected by potential construction suspension measures. On November 5, the market value of S&P 500 constituent stocks evaporated by about 3 trillion U.S. dollars in one day, and NVIDIA's share price fell by 9.26% in a single day. On November 6, the Korea Composite Index closed down 6.02%, and Zhongji Xuchuang fell by about 9% that day, closing at 448 yuan, down more than 67% from its year-to-date high in June.

Since November 9, personal turmoil of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang triggered market sell-offs, and within two trading days NVIDIA's market value evaporated by more than 430 billion U.S. dollars. The next day after November 5, the South Korean stock market triggered a decline circuit breaker during intraday trading. CoreWeave's business is to purchase NVIDIA GPUs, build data centers, and rent computing power to customers such as OpenAI, Microsoft and Meta according to contracts. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Tens of Millions Yuan Investment, Only 1.8M Box Office: Why Did the First AI-Generated Theatrical Film Flop?
stories.Summary:
Sanxingdui: Future Past, the first domestic theatrical film produced with AI technology, was released in Chinese cinemas on October 23 and has since struggled badly at the box office. The film is produced by Boyue Xingji Lantu companies under Bona Film Group, with Shengshu Technology providing AI technical support. By November 11, its cumulative box office had reached 1.802 million yuan. On November 12, its 21st day of release, 29 screenings were scheduled at 17 Beijing cinemas, yet not a single ticket had been sold by noon. The film has drawn wide attention because of its production method rather than its commercial results.

The film runs about 100 minutes and is set against the ancient Shu civilization of Sanxingdui and a future world. Iconic relics such as the Bronze Divine Tree, the Great Bronze Standing Figure and the Bronze Vertical Eye Mask appear throughout the story. In the plot, future humans depend too heavily on algorithms and fall into a global crisis, and the clues to solving it are hidden in ancient Shu inscriptions from 3,000 years ago. Its producer, Quji Xiaojiang, has said the production cost is in the tens of millions of yuan, while the same theme shot traditionally might cost 800 million to 900 million yuan. The team numbered nearly 100 people and spent two years on refinement, generating more than 1.2 million base maps.

The creative team has said that AI handles generation and execution work, while all creative conception and judgment are made by human creators. According to a reporter from Jiemian News, Shengshu Technology supplied computing power and worked on underlying problems such as enabling AI films to be shown on large screens, without interfering in creative decisions. Bona Film Group's Chief Administrative Officer, Jiang Defu, said AI saves part of the actors' shooting cost and shortens rendering time for some shots and large scenes. He also said the team's manpower and time costs have not fallen, and that technology iteration keeps generating costs. He stated that Bona did not treat box office as the primary goal, but wanted to test whether AI offers new solutions for the industry.

Audiences were largely unconvinced, and many one-star and two-star reviews on the film's Douban page are prominent. Critics said the picture lacks cinematic texture, that AI facial expressions are distorted, and that the dubbing fits the picture poorly. Others said the character lines carry a strong AI flavor and that the plot logic and narrative rhythm are chaotic. Most of the more positive reviews praised the producer's attempt at new technology and the combination of ancient Shu civilization with science fiction. The articles note that these criticisms split between problems tied to the model's generation ability and production process, and problems of character setting, lines and plot logic that fall to the creative team.

The film's start followed a clear pattern: its first three days of release, October 23 to 25, produced the highest box office, with single-day takings of 300,700 yuan, 464,400 yuan and 379,600 yuan. Audience numbers per screening were highest in those days, and takings then fell off sharply. The articles place the film within a wider trend, in which the film and television industry seeks lower costs and higher efficiency after the explosive growth of AI short dramas. On November 10, the Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival set up an AI unit for the first time, screening 20 works. A video Agent manufacturer told Jiemian News that its platform connects to Seedance, MiniMax H3 and Keling, with Seedance taking most calls, at a ratio of roughly 7:3 against MiniMax H3.

The articles leave several matters open. They do not say whether Sanxingdui: Future Past will remain on screens beyond its current schedule, or what its final box office will be. They do not give the revenue share that cinemas will take from the 1.8 million yuan already earned, nor how the gap to the disclosed production cost will be covered. Whether medium and long dramas and theatrical films will find the pioneers the articles say they need is not settled. The articles also do not state how Shengshu Technology's role will affect its wider commercial prospects.

stories.Headline: Are the massive layoffs at large corporations really caused by AI taking jobs away from humans?
stories.Summary:
Massive tech layoffs have been widely blamed on AI, but the data and company actions tell a more complicated story. U.S. initial jobless claims dropped to 189,000 in the latest data from the Department of Labor, matching the lowest level in 57 years. Challenger reported that October 2026 layoffs reached only 43,994 people, the lowest for the same period in three years. Reuters reported that Google has expanded voluntary separation packages to five overseas countries since June, with about 5,000 employees in Switzerland alone. Google's offer reaches up to 12 months of salary, and a week earlier Microsoft sent voluntary separation invitations to about 60,000 employees, a quarter of its headcount.

Companies prefer voluntary exits partly to avoid age discrimination lawsuits, since leavers must sign a waiver of the right to sue. Large U.S. layoffs also require notifying state governments 60 days in advance, which voluntary programs can sidestep. Challenger's statistics show tech layoffs this year exceeded 170,000 people, 20% above the same period last year. That figure ranks first among all industries and surpasses the roughly 168,000 tech layoffs of the full year 2001 dot-com bust. The broader U.S. job market remains strong, while the tech sector alone has cut more jobs than it did in 2001.

Responsibility for the cuts sits with the companies themselves, which have described them in terms of controlling costs amid heavy AI investment. Reuters reported that Google expanded its severance offers this year to control rising costs. Those who pursue the AI-replacement narrative include Goldman Sachs, whose March 2023 report estimated that about one-fifth of global jobs could be automated, equal to 300 million full-time positions. Citrini Research's hypothetical February report envisioned U.S. unemployment reaching 10.2% by June 2028. Its circulation coincided with the Dow falling 800 points on a Monday and IBM dropping 13% in one day.

Affected workers include senior employees, since Microsoft's April voluntary program targeted staff whose age plus tenure totaled at least 70 years, involving about 8,750 people. Oxford Economics found that in the first 11 months of 2025, only about 55,000 U.S. layoffs cited AI, 4.5% of the total, while poor market conditions caused four times as many. Official data show annualized U.S. labor productivity growth of only 0.8% and 1.4% in the first two quarters of 2026. Apollo's chief economist cited Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco data showing total factor productivity still slightly below zero. Meanwhile, Meta laid off about 8,000 people and moved about 7,000 to AI teams.

The narrative has deeper roots in media amplification, as headlines from The Independent and Chinese outlets repeated the 300 million jobs figure. Entrepreneur asked whether a viral AI doomsday report caused the Dow's drop. Real-world AI agent performance is limited, as the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI found the top model, Opus 5.5, reached professional-level results on only about 21% of 240 freelance projects. Mark Zuckerberg admitted in July that agent progress had not accelerated as expected. Several firms have also cut AI spending: Uber set a $1,500 monthly cap per employee for coding tools, and Tesla gave each employee a $200 weekly quota.

Future developments remain unclear from these articles, and the reporting leaves open how many of the voluntary separations will ultimately be completed. It is also unresolved whether AI-related layoffs will grow as agent capabilities improve, a question Andrej Karpathy suggested could take a decade to answer. The articles do not say whether companies will publicly revise their AI explanations for cuts. Whether the productivity data will show acceleration in later quarters is likewise not established. More to follow.

It also lists ways to transform underwriting and claims, strengthen fraud detection while protecting sensitive data, and build trust through explainability and auditability. NTT DATA's AI Factory is described as helping organizations move from isolated AI pilots to secure, governed AI at scale with measurable business outcomes. NTT DATA presents the research as showing how insurers scale AI with trust and control. The company says its AI Factory helps organizations move from isolated pilots to governed AI at scale. stories.Headline: Visure Launches Visure X for AI-Assisted Requirements Management
stories.Summary:
Visure Solutions announced the general availability of Visure X on November 13, 2026. The company launched this new platform from its headquarters in San Francisco. It provides AI-assisted requirements management for organizations developing safety-critical and regulated products. The software is available now for new customers and existing Visure Requirements ALM users. This next-generation experience was rebuilt from the ground up for large and complex programs.

The platform supports aerospace, defense, automotive, medical device, rail and industrial teams in San Francisco. It integrates requirements, models, risks, tests, and the wider PLM and CAD digital thread. Templates support frameworks including DO-178C, ISO 26262, ASPICE, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and EN 50128. Users can choose LLM providers via cloud, Microsoft Azure, Amazon Bedrock, or fully local models. Integration is enabled through ReqIF, SysML model import, webhooks, a REST API, and MCP.

Visure Solutions is a leading provider of requirements management and ALM software for regulated industries. The company stated that Visure X helps teams take products from concept to certification faster. They noted that the platform maintains the traceability and audit evidence that regulators expect. The company explained that the tool connects requirements to the wider digital thread through design. They claimed the system is significantly faster than the previous Visure Requirements ALM software.

Existing customers requested more speed on large projects, a simpler interface, and better parallel work support. Engineering organizations are under pressure to adopt AI but find generic assistants lack regulatory understanding. These teams often spend weeks reconstructing pictures by hand before every review or audit. Regulated programs are affected because generic AI output must still be checked, traced, and justified. The new system allows these teams to adopt AI within their own data-handling rules.

Safety-critical products now combine mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering across various suppliers and variants. Each engineering discipline typically works in its own tool, which creates fragmented information. A single requirement change can ripple into models, CAD, tests, hazard analyses, and certification evidence. Generic AI assistants do not understand an organization's specific information model, approval rules, or regulatory obligations. This environment makes it difficult to maintain a consistent digital thread during the development process.

Existing customers can contact their account managers to learn about various upgrade options for their systems. Interested parties can visit the company website at www.visuresolutions.com to request a product demonstration. Teams can move individual specifications at their own pace using a server-to-server import tool. The articles do not state the specific pricing for the new Visure X platform. They also leave open the specific timeline for future updates to the AI Agent.

stories.Headline: Google DeepMind AI agents reduce costs for attacking 1024-bit RSA keys
stories.Summary:
Google DeepMind has announced that AI agents, working under human supervision, found two ways to lower the cost of attacking 1024-bit RSA cryptosystems. The work was done with cryptographers from UC San Diego and Inria, and the results were reported on November 10, 2026. The findings suggest that attacks on legacy RSA-1024 need less computing effort than was previously assumed. The company says the results mainly affect these older systems. The first method concerns digital signatures and padding.

DeepMind found that if an attacker controls roughly half or more of a signed block, the padding gives no protection. The finding is especially relevant to the PKCS#1 v1.5 format used in devices such as hardware security modules. In a sandboxed test, the agents re-ran an earlier academic forgery attack on a 1024-bit key and cut the CPU time from 1,380 core-years to 391 core-years, a 3.5-fold improvement. Kohli, VP at Google DeepMind, noted that this signature attack does not recover the private key and requires around 4 billion signing queries made in advance.

The second method concerns factoring several RSA keys of the same size. The agents developed an algorithm that, on average, makes factoring each additional 1024-bit key about 30 times cheaper than previous methods. That estimate, however, assumes an initial computation as costly as factoring one key, and the method has not yet been implemented. Kohli stated that modern encryption protocols, which almost universally use 2048-bit or larger keys, remain secure.

The researchers concluded that cryptographic hardness cannot be treated as a fixed assumption in an era of AI-enabled computation. The researchers emphasised that using AI to rigorously test long-held assumptions will help ensure the security of modern encryption. The articles do not say what steps are planned for operators of legacy 1024-bit systems. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Google DeepMind’s AI Agents Make 1024-Bit RSA Keys Cheaper to Attack - SecurityWeek

stories.Headline: China’s Jensen Huang ‘honeypot’ trap is only more reason to win the AI race
stories.Summary:
China's Jensen Huang, the Nvidia chief executive, has been at the centre of a controversy over an alleged extra-marital affair and claims that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy. Commentators and social media have turned the saga into widespread entertainment, with memes and influencer gags spreading online. The matter has also prompted questions about its effect on the frontier artificial intelligence race between the United States and China. Analysts see the episode as a potential shift in that contest, one that could influence how the two countries compete in AI development. The coverage gives the story a central place in the wider debate over AI leadership.

Huang has long been seen as a villain by many US hawks because he has argued for relaxing restrictions on the sale of Nvidia chips to China. The latest allegations have added to hawkish views about him, and the scrutiny extends to concerns over alleged corporate espionage. An HT analysis of trade data shows China has rising import dependence on commodities that are likely GPUs or related products. The United States has tried to restrict China's access to cutting-edge chips and GPUs, while China has limited rare earth mineral supplies to the US. The Pax Silica alliance, launched by the US in December 2025, is designed to ease American access to rare earth minerals.

China has denied the allegations of spying and has downplayed the controversy, as expected. The Straits Times writer argues that some pain for Nvidia could help secure the West's AI lead over China in the long run. Commentators disagree on how much China needs Nvidia's chips, and the actual evidence on that question is not clear. The HT analysis notes that the disclosure of Huang's affair is certain to add paranoia in the US AI ecosystem about a Chinese catch-up. The writer's view is that Nvidia's weakening might also spur competition and innovation.

China's trade surplus is expected to exceed a trillion dollars for a second consecutive year in 2026, according to the HT report. China released the open-source reasoning model DeepSeek-R1 in January 2025, bringing it within striking distance of leading frontier AI developers, all based in the US. A Lowy Institute report shows Chinese models are catching up fast with American models, although the US leads China in every AI field except human resources. A Carnegie China report, cited by HT, indicates China is catching up quickly with the US in skilled AI workforce. Huawei announced a new chip-design approach in May 2026 that could limit the effect of US export controls.

The articles leave open whether the constraints on chips and rare earths will matter in the long term, and whether either side will crack its challenge before those constraints become redundant. The Lowy Institute report says Huawei could design chips by 2031 with transistor density equivalent to TSMC's 2028 chips, but whether this succeeds is not yet known. Beijing countered the Pax Silica alliance with the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization earlier in 2026. The articles do not say how the allegations against Huang will ultimately be resolved or how Nvidia's position will change.

stories.Headline: Consumer-first thinking, enterprise AI: Why Tencent Cloud wants adoption to feel like ‘turning on a light’
stories.Summary:
Tencent Cloud is promoting its enterprise AI tools, including the WorkBuddy office productivity agent and PalmAI palm recognition, according to a Business Times branded article published on November 13, 2026. WorkBuddy helps employees analyse information, prepare documents and complete tasks across applications, and it selects a suitable large language model for each task. Since its launch in March 2026, WorkBuddy has rolled out more than 100 updates, a possibility driven through the use of AI. In Singapore, local company Weesware has applied Tencent Cloud's PalmAI to senior activity centres through its CaritaHub platform. More than 10,000 seniors can now sign in without cards or passcodes using contactless palm recognition.

Tencent Cloud combines its tools with consulting and implementation support, and its consultants across Asia-Pacific markets work alongside businesses to identify suitable AI applications. Its Consulting-as-a-Service is described as high-touch, giving businesses an expert to call about their AI needs and to guide their AI strategy. Tencent Cloud places forward-deployed engineers directly within client teams to deliver tailored solutions and steer clear of one-size-fits-all deployments. In Indonesia, Tencent Cloud was the strategic technology partner for telecommunications operator XLSMART on a large-scale cloud migration. Tencent Cloud developed more than 20 AI-assisted migration tools using WorkBuddy and AI coding assistant CodeBuddy, moving 1,200 microservices and over 15 terabytes of core data in four and a half months with zero downtime.

Poshu Yeung, senior vice president of Tencent Cloud and head of Tencent Cloud International, compared enterprise AI to electricity, saying you turn on the switch and see the light without asking where it comes from. Yeung said Tencent has a lot of To-C DNA, and that DNA now comes in handy, referring to consumer-first thinking. He said AI is moving fast, but the priority is ensuring it is deployed practically to create real, positive impact for the communities served. Yeung said enterprises must first understand where the technology can address their operational needs rather than adopting AI simply because it is available. He said that with AI tools, adoption of advanced technologies can happen easily and seamlessly with the right price performance for businesses to grow alongside evolving tech ecosystems.

Tencent Cloud reported in October this year that its active overseas customer base had doubled over the preceding year, while international demand for its AI solutions had grown at a triple-digit rate. The approach draws on Tencent's more than 20 years of developing consumer services, including Weixin and its international version WeChat, which together have 1.4 billion monthly users. Tencent Cloud's parent company has been developing and deploying its AI capabilities since 2016. CodeBuddy was first developed for use in-house and was tried and tested internally by employees in real-world internal workflows.

WorkBuddy is developed from real-world internal use cases and shaped by continuous feedback across the company's ecosystem. Many companies in Asia-Pacific are still working out where AI can improve their operations, while grappling with ageing IT systems, fragmented data and regulatory requirements. Potential applications include repetitive processes in human resources, finance, procurement and legal operations, but wider adoption also depends on modernising legacy systems and connecting fragmented data. Tencent Cloud's AI CAN DO IT hackathon programme has drawn more than 10,000 participants across five markets in the past six months.

The Singapore edition was co-organised with AI Singapore, and participants tackled real challenges from partners such as DBS, Keppel, Aspire, Ryde and NTU's Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine. Challenges ranged from capturing employees' expertise for others to draw on to helping patients manage their health. Looking to 2027, Tencent Cloud plans to expand its international AI solutions and strengthen their global infrastructure, helping businesses manage the cost of their digital transformation. The article does not say how much the tools or consulting services cost.

It does not name the senior activity centres in Singapore that use PalmAI. It does not give the value or terms of the XLSMART migration contract. It does not say which five markets hosted the hackathon programme. It does not specify what infrastructure Tencent Cloud plans to strengthen in 2027.

stories.Headline: Resorts World Sentosa, Honeywell launch AI-powered district cooling initiatives
stories.Summary:
Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) will become the first tourism destination in Singapore to adopt artificial intelligence-powered technologies for district cooling, according to a report published on November 3, 2026. The integrated resort unveiled the plan as a "co-innovation initiative" with Honeywell Technologies, a pure-play automation company. The programme will deploy predictive optimisation technologies that anticipate cooling demand, reduce energy use and keep guests comfortable. Such technologies combine AI forecasts with optimisation algorithms to predict future conditions and choose the best actions. Cooling is one of the largest and most complex energy demands at a facility of RWS's size.

The initiative covers three programmes. First, smart air-conditioning systems that continuously adjust output to match actual cooling demand are expected to cut energy use in the resort's hotel rooms by 20 to 30 per cent. Second, AI-based predictive optimisation is estimated to save about 5 to 10 per cent of energy in the Resorts World Convention Centre and Minion Land at Universal Studios Singapore. Third, a predictive district cooling plant will forecast how much cooling is needed and decide which equipment should run and when, which should reduce excess chilled water production. Using Honeywell's Forge platform, energy data will also be turned into insights that flag waste and recommend fixes.

RWS projects annual energy savings of two gigawatt-hours from the combined measures, equal to the yearly electricity use of about 438 four-room public housing flats. RWS and Honeywell are jointly responsible for the initiative, which builds on a cloud-based foundation for building operations the two organisations set up in 2023. Kess Chiang, senior vice-president of resort services at RWS, said facilities management should go beyond fixing equipment after it breaks and use technology to stay ahead. Chiang said the aim is for guests never to feel too hot or too cold while using only the energy needed. Munish Suri, president of building automation at Honeywell Technologies for India and Asia-Pacific, said interconnected systems that optimise energy use as conditions change will be the next frontier in building efficiency.

He added that RWS shows sustainability and operational excellence can strengthen the guest experience rather than compete with it. The technologies were developed and tested in a hospitality setting through a Honeywell Centre of Excellence, which was set up with support from the Singapore Economic Development Board. The initiative supports RWS's goal of becoming carbon-neutral by 2030. The report does not say when the new systems will be fully deployed, and it does not give a cost for the programme.

stories.Headline: ArcticRAT Cybercrime Gang Profiles Victim Finances With AI
stories.Summary:
Zimperium researchers reported on November 13, 2026 that the ArcticRAT cybercrime gang had turned its Android malware from a cryptocurrency stealer into a full remote access Trojan. The operators added large language model services to sift stolen text messages for financial data worth exploiting. Zimperium called the change a dangerous escalation in the mobile threat landscape. The newer versions let attackers interact with infected devices in real time instead of relying on hardcoded actions. The gang used malvertising, smishing and third-party forums to send visitors to malicious websites carrying the malware.

Early ArcticRAT versions targeted users of 11 specific cryptocurrency applications to harvest data for access to crypto accounts. The new versions add remote device control and surveillance, credential and keystroke theft, screen capture, live screen streaming, microphone monitoring, and theft of SMS messages, contacts and call logs. Attackers can also steal or change lock-screen credentials, potentially locking victims out of their devices. Since July, Zimperium identified 78 unique malware samples, 42 dropper samples, 36 payloads and 21 IP addresses used for command-and-control communications. The researchers also found 129 distinct commands for remotely controlling infected devices, stealing information, monitoring activity and manipulating device functions.

Nico Chiaraviglio, chief scientist at Zimperium, said ArcticRAT uses AI to read user information such as SMS messages to filter for financial information that could be used to perform fraud. He said one particularly challenging technique is hidden remote control combined with a black-screen overlay, with attackers abusing legitimate Android features while making the device appear locked or powered off. He said defending against such threats requires AI-powered on-device threat detection, controls over application installation and permissions, and runtime application protection to spot suspicious screen-sharing activity and malicious overlays. Zimperium said the primary attack vector relied on a landing page that convincingly impersonated Google Play to trick targets into downloading a malicious application. The researchers observed attackers in some instances using Amazon Web Services storage buckets to deliver the payload directly on Android devices.

Zimperium found the malware features an API connection to xAI's Grok model, which attackers can activate remotely to examine installed applications and identify banking, cryptocurrency and trading platforms. The AI capabilities let ArcticRAT process stolen SMS messages and separate routine and promotional messages from one-time authentication codes, account balance changes and transaction notifications. It can even estimate a victim's financial standing before sending the information to its command-and-control infrastructure, according to Zimperium. The firm said this automates much of the work of sorting large volumes of stolen information rather than manually examining the data. Zimperium said that as mobile Trojan threats like ArcticRAT become increasingly sophisticated, conventional signature-based security layers are no longer sufficient to protect enterprise mobile endpoints.

Once installed, the latest version abuses Android Accessibility Services permissions to connect with its command-and-control servers, giving attackers remote control over the device. The malware first collects information about the compromised device, including its location, battery status, screen state, Wi-Fi connectivity and currently active applications. It sends that information to the attackers, who can then select which functions to activate based on the victim's device and installed applications. The malware uses a completely black, un-dismissible screen overlay to conceal attacker activities from victims. Analysts noted the trend underscores the need for users and organizations to stop treating mobile devices as secondary security concerns and to apply the same threat monitoring, access controls and protections as for traditional endpoints.

The article was written by Illinois-based Jai Vijayan, a veteran technology journalist with more than 25 years of experience covering cybersecurity. Zimperium is tracking the malware and described the evolution as an example of how quickly mobile threats are evolving, with attackers using AI to make malware more capable and dangerous. The article gives no indication of how many victims have been infected or where they are located. It does not say whether law enforcement or Google has taken any action against the gang or its infrastructure. It also does not say what the attackers do with the financial intelligence after it reaches their command-and-control servers.

Articles.Title: ArcticRAT Cybercrime Gang Profiles Victim Finances With AI - Dark Reading

stories.Headline: Researchers in Australia develop AI tool to identify dangerous rip currents - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Researchers in Australia have developed an AI-powered mobile tool that can identify potential rip currents from beach photographs, according to a statement from the University of New South Wales released Wednesday. The project, called RipEye, pairs the image analysis tool, which can flag potential rip currents within seconds, with an interactive game meant to teach people how to spot the dangerous currents. Xinhua reported the announcement from Sydney on November 12. The articles do not say who funded the work or how many people were involved.

Rip currents remain one of Australia's deadliest beach hazards, and the 2025 National Drowning Report attributes 47 percent of the 66 beach drowning deaths recorded that year to them. The researchers trained the AI model on thousands of beach images, including more than 10,000 images of rip currents collected at different beaches. In testing, the tool correctly detected a rip about 80 percent of the time. The researchers stressed, however, that the tool cannot guarantee that an area of water is safe.

The tool will be trialed this summer with selected clubs from Surf Life Saving Australia. The articles say the longer-term aim is to use it to support public beach safety education and lifesaving operations. They do not specify how many clubs will take part or when results of the trial will be published. The articles also do not give details on how the tool will be made available to the public.

The lifesaving organization and the university team are the parties named in the articles, and the researchers' own caution about the tool's limits is the main stated position. The 80 percent detection rate means the remaining cases go undetected, which the researchers acknowledged by saying the tool cannot promise safety. The articles do not include comment from any beachgoer, government body, or independent expert. Beyond the summer trial, the articles offer no further timeline or next steps.
