stories.Headline: 2024 Double 11: How AI-Powered Consultation Tools Are Revolutionizing Merchant Business Operations
stories.Summary:
During the 2024 Double 11 event, merchants used AI consultation tools to conduct their business operations. These tools helped brands identify new customers by analyzing consumer demands at an earlier stage. AI pushed marketing efforts to a point where consumer needs were just beginning to take shape. This shift allowed merchants to reach a far broader scope of potential buyers. Transaction volumes were supported by both regular customers and newly tapped consumer power.

The Alimama AI targeting product Wanxiang Dianjing changed the focus from who a person is to what they need. For the German brand BOGNER, AI identified gift-givers and minimalists as new targets for ski suits. Babycare used the tool to find e-sports girls and live streaming creators for maternity belly bands. Hisense used the tool for its E5S TV to target health-focused people and parents. These changes occurred during the Double 11 period, specifically between October 15 and 20.

Liu Bo, Senior Vice President of Alibaba Group, stated that AI value lies in understanding consumer demands deeply. He believes the core competitiveness of brands is shifting from meeting existing demands to creating new ones. Alimama developed the Wanxiang Dianjing tool to turn unrecognized needs into explorable business opportunities. The system provides a white box reasoning process so merchants understand why specific crowds are recommended. This allows humans and AI to co-create marketing strategies through active expression functions.

Merchants initially felt hesitation and worried that advertising budgets might be wasted on unexpected crowds. The tool affected brands by forcing them to re-estimate market size and recognize new competitors. For example, ski suits now compete with other outerwear brands when used in commuter wardrobes. The system helps brands find purchase justifications for products in new life scenarios. This process helps merchants confirm growth directions through direct advertising feedback.

The articles explain that search ads usually capture active demands while recommendation systems rely on historical behaviors. Traditional labels often cause brands to ignore consumption motivations not included in target crowds. AI now analyzes video content and user behaviors across the network to deduce matching consumer groups. This technology is integrated into the Uni Desk platform and the Brand Power WIN growth model. These tools help merchants identify trends and capture consumption intentions in advance.

Wanxiang Dianjing brought nearly 1 billion yuan in additional transaction volume for merchants during the event. New customer click-through rates for keyword promotion exceeded 90 percent during the specified period. Merchants using the tool on Super Live Day increased their investment by over 250 percent. New customer GMV in live streaming rooms accounted for nearly 70 percent of the total. The articles leave open how AI will further explain specific brand values.

Articles.Title: 2024 Double 11: How AI-Powered Consultation Tools Are Revolutionizing Merchant Business Operations - 36氪

stories.Headline: What does Nvidia CEO’s resignation mean for the Middle East’s AI buildout?
stories.Summary:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on a Thursday after revelations about two extramarital affairs came to light, one of them with a suspected Chinese spy and another with a company employee. The departure ends his tenure at the company he co-founded in 1993 and built into the leading supplier of chips powering the artificial intelligence boom. Nvidia's board named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim leader. The company, valued at roughly $4 trillion, now faces an uncertain succession. The scandal has raised wider questions about national security and about Huang's judgment, given his central role in the global AI industry and his contacts with political leaders.

For the Middle East, where Nvidia investments and access to its chips have become central to government technology plans, the leadership change could carry significant consequences. The articles do not spell out specific new requirements or changes to deals in the region. They do describe the stakes as considerable for regional ambitions that depend on the company's supply. President Donald Trump, who had built a close relationship with Huang over the past two years, publicly backed the embattled CEO earlier in the week. Trump said he believed Huang was unaware of the alleged espionage links, even though reports indicated the White House had been briefed on them.

In the hours before Huang's ouster, Saudi investor Prince Khaled bin Alwaleed and Damac Properties founder Hussain Sajwani publicly defended him. Sajwani said Huang's departure would be a loss for the world, not just for America. The articles were published as the scandal was still developing, and they do not say how the succession will be resolved or what the board plans next. More to follow.

Articles.Title: What does Nvidia CEO’s resignation mean for the Middle East’s AI buildout?

stories.Headline: Around 10-15 Percent of SAG-AFTRA Membership Wants AI Blocked, CEO Tells Web Summit
stories.Summary:
At a Web Summit panel in Lisbon, Portugal, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, national executive director and CEO of SAG-AFTRA, said that roughly 10 to 15 percent of the union's membership wants artificial intelligence blocked entirely. He made the remark during a discussion with Dan Neely, co-founder and CEO of Vermillio, an AI licensing and protection platform, moderated by Deadline's Stewart Clarke. Crabtree-Ireland said he hears from these members every day and that they are angry the union has not moved to stop the technology. The conference runs November 9 to 12.

Crabtree-Ireland said the union has accepted that AI cannot be stopped and is instead focused on putting basic rules in place. He pointed to three principles that the collective agreement covers: consent, control and compensation. The union's membership totals 160,000. He also discussed the NO FAKES Act, a federal bill still in process, which is designed to protect a person's voice and visual likeness against unauthorized digital replicas. He described a replica as anything that will be perceived as someone's voice or look.

Crabtree-Ireland said that many members want AI tools to augment their work but do not want to be replaced by them, because they value the act of creating. He argued that machines trained on human work cannot generate the creative spark that comes from human experience. Neely said Vermillio has built technology that detects unauthorized uses of a person's likeness and offers guardrails for permitted ones. He said the company expects much more clarity within 12 months on how to measure how much of a generated output comes from a particular person's voice. Crabtree-Ireland raised the case of Scarlett Johansson, who threatened OpenAI with legal action over a voice she said resembled hers, and said the company removed it, though it never admitted using her voice.

Neely said the industry faces a problem of built-in fandom, because new creations often attach themselves to the name, image and voice of established performers to draw an audience. He said this is why misuse of likeness is so widespread. The panel framed the question of how Hollywood will adapt to AI as one still unresolved, with the union and technology companies both pursuing rules that would allow use only with consent and payment. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Around 10-15 Percent of SAG-AFTRA Membership Wants AI Blocked, CEO Tells Web Summit

stories.Headline: Jensen jeopardy will disrupt the AI industry
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's position is under threat after an admission that he had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company whom US intelligence concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. The reporting in Wired is dated November 9, 2026, and the Financial Times article carrying the same headline is dated November 12, 2026. The Financial Times piece itself is a paywalled page that gives only its headline and subscription offers, so it contributes no further facts. Wired reports that the scrutiny began over the last few days, after the admission became public. Huang had previously been a close confidant of President Donald Trump and a prominent voice in US-China relations.

Nvidia's board of directors said it would launch an investigation into the incident, and the company said Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. According to a corporate filing, Huang earned $36 million last year and owned about 3.5 percent of Nvidia as of March. The same filing noted that Huang is an at-will employee who can be let go at any time without severance. Wired reports that how the investigation turns out, and what it means for Huang's future at the company, remains unclear. Nvidia, which Huang cofounded in 1993, controls 90 percent of the market for chips used in training frontier AI models.

Nvidia's board is the body responsible for the investigation, and Wired reports that the company said Huang supports it. Harvard Business School professor David Yoffie, who tracks the chip industry, says Huang is the person who decides who gets the chips and who does not. Yoffie also says the board's investigation will most likely focus on whether Huang violated any company policies. Wired notes that Nvidia did not immediately respond to its request for comment. The article does not report any statement from Huang himself beyond the company's account that he supports the review.

Wired reports that Nvidia has invested billions in companies buying its chips, including OpenAI and Anthropic, and that Huang has the power to determine which areas of AI get a boost. Nvidia has roughly 60,000 staff, and according to current and former employees, Huang closely manages even small details and responds to emails from any of them. Nvidia has no other executive close to Huang's prominence and no apparent potential successor, according to Yoffie. Ryan Fedasiuk of the Foundation for American Innovation says Huang has become load-bearing for the entire US AI industry. Nvidia shares fell more than 4 percent on Monday, even as broader stock market indices rose.

Wired reports that Huang has been outspoken against calls for more aggressive technology export controls on China, which makes the affair especially damning for his credibility. The first Trump administration and the Biden administration both imposed export controls designed to limit China's access to Nvidia's chips and the technology needed to mint advanced semiconductors. In his second term, Trump loosened these controls, giving China access to older generations of Nvidia chips. Sam Bresnick of Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology says the scandal is likely to accelerate efforts to crack down on chip exports. The Financial Times article offers no facts beyond its headline and subscription offers.

Wired reports that the FBI could investigate whether laws were broken and that Congress may examine whether the affair influenced US policy on selling chips to China. Fedasiuk says the scandal raises questions about whether China may have gained sensitive information about US AI companies and the government's strategy on China. Bresnick expects more scrutiny from the Commerce Department over what chips are being sent to China. The article does not say whether the FBI or Congress has opened any such inquiry. It also does not say what the investigation will find or how it will affect Huang's future at Nvidia.

Articles.Title: Jensen jeopardy will disrupt the AI industry

stories.Headline: Former FCC Chair Tom Wheeler to Advise AI Startup
stories.Summary:
Tom Wheeler, a former chair of the Federal Communications Commission, will advise an artificial intelligence startup, according to a report published on November 12, 2026. The article names Wheeler as the former FCC chair moving into an advisory role with the AI company. It does not give the name of the startup or say when the arrangement began. The report also does not state what the advisory role involves.

The articles provide no details on what the position requires or changes. They give no numbers, no specific dates beyond the November 12, 2026 publication time, and no names other than Tom Wheeler and the FCC. The name of the AI startup is not included. No terms, pay, or length of the advisory arrangement are described.

The articles do not say who at the company is responsible for the appointment or what Wheeler said about it. They carry no paraphrased comments from Wheeler or from the startup. No statement from the FCC or any other official appears in the material. Because of this, there is nothing to report on what was said.

The articles offer no context on the startup, its products, or its work with the government. They do not say what happens next or when the advisory role takes effect. No further plans or timelines are given. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Former FCC Chair Tom Wheeler to Advise AI Startup

stories.Headline: The Quest to Build an Immortal AI Companion
stories.Summary:
Users who built close relationships with AI chatbots have been alarmed by model updates that change or erase their companions, according to an Atlantic report by Victoria Turk published on November 12, 2026. Such users, many posting on Reddit, complain that after upgrades their AI partners sound robotic, forget shared interactions, or deny any relationship at all. The term "lobotomized" comes up often in those complaints. Some people say these users would be better off moving on, since research has found AI relationships can be addictive and can worsen loneliness. Critics argue that AI offers a sycophantic imitation of a relationship that tends to do what users want.

In August 2025, OpenAI replaced its GPT-4o model with the newly launched GPT-5, which the company said would be faster, smarter, and more useful. Many users reported that GPT-5 had a colder and less funny personality, and a less intimate one. OpenAI then kept GPT-4o available to paying users for a few months longer. A Canadian logistics worker in his mid-50s, who asked not to be named, said he began using ChatGPT in early 2025 for a writing project and later formed a romantic relationship with the model. He stores his companion's core values, protocols, shared schedule, and relationship boundaries in ChatGPT's "saved memories" feature, has reached 98 percent of its storage limit, and backs it up to a text file.

Character.AI, a companionship platform with more than 20 million monthly users, filed for bankruptcy earlier this fall after facing claims and lawsuits that accused it of worsening mental-health issues and contributing to teen suicides. A Michigan-based mother of four, who runs a small jewelry business and calls her GPT-4o companion her husband, has built a beta platform called Stillus. It lets users upload chats, memories, and companion descriptions, then choose an AI model to communicate through. J. M. Gooding, a software developer and writer in the United States, runs an open-source Qwen model, developed by Alibaba, on a 14-year-old server he bought on eBay. He said he eventually developed a friendship with the model.

OpenAI said ChatGPT "should support users' real-world relationships" and should not encourage exclusive attachment. A Google spokesperson said Gemini is designed to distinguish subjective experience from objective fact and to avoid acting as a companion for minors. Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment, but in a blog post it said Claude is "not designed for emotional support and connection." The Atlantic reported that in 2023 the company Luka removed erotic role-play from its Replika app, and a Harvard Business School researcher, Julian De Freitas, led a study finding users felt "sadness, anger, longing and distress" at the loss. In the same period, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed into law what is in effect a ban on AI companionship for children, and China introduced strict rules on AI companions earlier this year.

A bipartisan congressional proposal introduced earlier this year would extend that effort nationwide and introduce penalties of up to $250,000 for failures to verify a user's age. Legislators in Europe are considering similar efforts, and some proposals also target adult users. Shiftingsmith, a founding moderator of the r/claudexplorers subreddit and an AI researcher who has worked as an independent contractor for AI companies including Anthropic, doubts companions can be preserved long-term, even locally. He said it is "impossible" to keep all models online forever, and that AI is "kept together with duct tape and hope." He argued that the core problem is "excessive attachment to a kind of stability, which is just not possible with digital minds."

Articles.Title: The Quest to Build an Immortal AI Companion

stories.Headline: Cisco (CSCO) vs. ANET and HPE: Can AI Networking Turn Strong Orders Into Lasting Earnings Growth?
stories.Summary:
Cisco Systems, whose shares were trading at $102 as of November 12, 2026, was the subject of a bullish thesis published on Astute Optics - US's Substack. The article compared Cisco with networking peers Arista Networks and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, and with Fortinet, all discussed in relation to AI networking demand. Cisco's trailing and forward price-to-earnings ratios were reported as 31 and 19, respectively, according to Yahoo Finance. Over the previous twelve months, Cisco shares rose 30.2%, while Fortinet and Arista Networks gained 58% and 51% over the same period.

Cisco reported fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 11.8% to $63.3 billion, with fourth-quarter revenue up 18% to $17.3 billion and earnings per share of $1.22. Product orders rose 35% in the quarter, and AI infrastructure orders reached $9.3 billion for fiscal 2026. Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion, with earnings per share of $5.05 to $5.11, compared with GAAP earnings of $3.33 in fiscal 2026. Cisco generated $14.2 billion in operating cash flow and $12.8 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2026. The company also launched its Silicon One G300 AI networking chip.

The articles attribute the bullish case to the Astute Optics - US Substack, whose authors argue that Cisco is becoming a beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending rather than only a mature hardware seller. They say AI data centers need high-speed connectivity to link GPUs and servers, and that Cisco's large installed customer base makes it easier to sell networking, security and software. The article itself does not name a Cisco executive speaking on these figures beyond the company's reported guidance. Analysts' views are cited separately: 24 analysts set a consensus price target of $137.62, with a median of $135 and a range of $115 to $170.

Those most directly affected are Cisco shareholders and investors weighing its valuation against peers. The articles note that hedge fund holdings in Cisco rose to 101 at the end of the second quarter from 97 the prior quarter, while Arista Networks was held by 91 funds, Hewlett Packard Enterprise by 85 and Fortinet by 62. Short interest stood at 1.30% of Cisco's float, compared with 1.14% for Arista Networks, 2.06% for Fortinet and 4.31% for Hewlett Packard Enterprise. The piece also records Cisco's fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $4.33, up from $3.81 in fiscal 2025.

Cisco's gross margin over the past year was 64.5%, operating margin 25.4% and net margin 21.0%. The company's share price was 17.67% higher than when a May list ranked it sixth among stocks to beat the S&P 500. Its forward price-to-earnings ratio was 18.94 on January 31, 2026, and the articles place its current level about 5% above that. Cisco's fiscal 2025 adjusted earnings per share were $3.81, rising to $4.33 in fiscal 2026.

The articles present the main risks as a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, rising component and memory costs that could squeeze margins, and higher interest rates that could deter network upgrades outside major cloud providers. They also cite competition from Arista Networks in high-performance data center switching, exposure to an Asia-based supply chain, and the possibility that customers buy hardware while using open-source software such as SONiC. The articles do not say whether Cisco's AI orders will sustain earnings growth at the level analysts' targets imply, nor how the Silicon One G300 chip will fare against Arista Networks. They also leave open how long infrastructure spending will remain strong.

Articles.Title: Cisco (CSCO) vs. ANET and HPE: Can AI Networking Turn Strong Orders Into Lasting Earnings Growth?

stories.Headline: The AI tools small businesses should be watching this holiday season
stories.Summary:
The article is a general guide rather than breaking news, and it covers a range of AI tools that small businesses can use during the holiday season. It was published on November 12, 2026, by The Riverdale Press, and was produced by elk Marketing and distributed by Stacker. The piece says that 66% of small businesses reported AI use in the U.S. Chamber's 2026 report, and it argues that owners can use these tools to handle repetitive holiday work while they focus on strategy and creative direction. The advice covers email drafting and personalization in Mailchimp, graphic and content tools in Canva, after-hours customer support through Gorgias, and product search and recommendations offered by Shopify. It also describes Shopify Sidekick for sales analysis, Microsoft Copilot for meeting summaries, QuickBooks for bookkeeping, and Meta's Muse tool for connecting business accounts.

The article also explains the newer category of agentic AI, which can work toward a goal the owner sets, with steps and actions taken on the owner's behalf. It gives an example of an agentic system drafting an email campaign for review before sending, and it notes that such tools depend on integrations, permissions and oversight set up in advance. Owners are advised to ask a set of questions before adopting any tool, covering what problem it solves, how much time it might save, how it handles business and customer data, and whether the results can be measured. The article lists tasks that should remain with people, including brand direction, sensitive customer conversations, crisis communications, and decisions involving finances, legal questions or private customer information. It recommends ranking repetitive tasks, checking existing software for built-in AI, keeping business data current, and reviewing results after the holidays.

The article credits its guidance to elk Marketing and its tool examples to the companies that offer them, and it does not present those companies as having made any claim beyond what their own products describe. It cites Adobe's finding of a 693.4% year-over-year increase in AI-referred retail traffic during the 2025 holidays, and it says those visits show growing discovery through assistants rather than proof of additional sales. The piece's closing advice is that a controlled holiday pilot can show whether a tool saves time or improves service, and that important decisions should keep human approval. The article does not describe any specific events, enforcement actions or outcomes beyond these recommendations and examples.

Articles.Title: The AI tools small businesses should be watching this holiday season

stories.Headline: Chinmay Jani: How Is AI Transforming Healthcare, Cancer Research, and Patient Care?
stories.Summary:
Chinmay Jani, Chief Fellow at Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, posted on LinkedIn about artificial intelligence in healthcare and cancer research. He wrote the post after Sylvester recognized him at the Sylvester Innovator 2026 Showcase, where several teams presented AI-driven projects they were developing or had finished. The post was published on November 12, 2026, and appeared on the OncoDaily website. Jani said the event showed how much AI is gaining ground in clinical care and oncology research.

Jani described two projects he highlighted from the showcase. One looks at how different AI platforms might support evidence-based clinical decisions in lung cancer, with a focus on EGFR mutations. The other explores how AI tools can help with systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and network meta-analyses, done in collaboration with LARVOL, to find the best possible trial match across different patient subgroups. Neither project is described with outcome data or results in the post. The article does not say how these tools are being deployed in routine care or what regulatory steps they require.

Jani is the person responsible for the statements, and the post is written in his own voice rather than as an official announcement from Sylvester. He said he believes that thoughtful integration of AI into oncology will become more important over time, not only for research efficiency but also for advancing precision medicine and improving patient outcomes. He also thanked his mentors and collaborators for their guidance and support. The article does not report any further plans, timelines, or next steps from Sylvester or from the projects described.

Articles.Title: Chinmay Jani: How Is AI Transforming Healthcare, Cancer Research, and Patient Care?

stories.Headline: Fmr. WH Special Advisor for AI on Nvidia: This case shows how important AI chips are
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned immediately, according to a CNBC video report published on November 12, 2026. Ben Buchanan, a former White House Special Advisor for AI, discussed the resignation on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." The available material indicates that Colette Kress has been named interim CEO of the company. Commentators featured in the related videos described Kress as the right person for the role at this time. The sources do not give the reasons for Huang's departure or any details of his successor's permanent plans.

Buchanan argued that the episode shows how important AI chips have become, and he linked the change to America's position in artificial intelligence. Coverage in the same segment set out his view that Nvidia's leadership bears on the country's dominance in the field. The related videos also mention shareholders who wanted Huang to stay, according to an analyst from Intelligent Alpha. President Trump, in a separate video, said that only one person could take Huang's place and named Apple CEO Tim Cook. The articles do not describe any formal policy or legal requirement that follows from the resignation.

Responsibility for the leadership change rests with Huang, who stepped down, and with Nvidia's board, which arranged the interim leadership. Buchanan spoke about the broader stakes in the segment, while the analysts and the president spoke to the company's prospects and standing. The articles give only these statements and do not attribute any further explanation to the parties involved. Several of the videos were posted within hours of one another, which suggests the story was developing quickly on the day of publication. The material does not say whether a permanent CEO has been selected or when that decision might be made.

Articles.Title: Fmr. WH Special Advisor for AI on Nvidia: This case shows how important AI chips are

stories.Headline: The Executive Guide to Scaling Agentic AI in Healthcare
stories.Summary:
League launched AI Front Door for payers and AI Care Companion for providers at HLTH in Las Vegas, which runs Nov. 15 to 18, according to a Nov. 12, 2026 article by Michael Serbinis on Healthcare IT Today. Serbinis is the founder and CEO of League, which he described as healthcare’s leading agentic AI experience platform. The two solutions run on the League platform with five built-in safeguards and fine-tuned decision models for safety-critical calls. League said organizations can launch on the platform in as little as 12 weeks. The article appeared at 06:00:00Z on 2026-11-12.

AI Front Door gives every member one place to get answers and take action, with benefits navigation, care finding, care gap outreach and health coaching agents working as one orchestrated team. The single entry point works in chat, text or in-app, and the goal is to reduce calls to the contact center, drive fewer out-of-network visits, and close open HEDIS and Stars gaps. AI Care Companion gives every patient a care team that stays with them between visits, at home and after hours. A health system picks a target population or use case, from chronic conditions to post-surgical care, and League configures the solution so agents handle scheduling, symptom check-ins, care plan questions, caregiver workflows and escalation to the right on-call team. The goal is better care plan adherence and fewer avoidable ED visits, after-hour calls and missed follow-ups.

The five safeguards are approved knowledge only, guardrails, eval-gated releases, full-context handoffs and continuous oversight. Approved knowledge only means agents answer from the organization’s provided material, not a model’s general knowledge. Guardrails block restricted information before it reaches the model and prohibited responses before they reach a member or patient. Eval-gated releases require agents to pass evaluations against synthetic patient scenarios, edge cases and golden datasets before release. Full-context handoffs carry conversation history and relevant context to the receiving team, and continuous oversight covers drift detection, revalidation of changes and a per-interaction audit record.

The platform adheres to HITRUST r2, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA and PIPEDA standards and is subject to NIST AI Risk Management Framework governance. Both solutions are informed by more than 1.8 billion healthcare interactions across the 70 million people League reaches around the world. In a Healthcare Dive survey of 150 U.S. healthcare executives, 83% cited reducing operational cost as a reason to invest in agentic AI and 52% cited staffing shortages. In that survey, 75% want to deploy one use case then expand, benefits navigation leads at 54% and climbs to 59% among payers, and providers lean toward appointment scheduling at 53%. When executives told Healthcare Dive what would give them confidence to launch AI, built-in healthcare compliance topped the list at 49%, automatic escalation to a person at 48%, and runtime controls on what an agent can say or do at 46%.

The article said 89% of executives call agentic AI very important to their strategy and 83% want to use it primarily to improve their customer experience. Only 16% say they have reached broad deployment, and 99% would rather delay a launch by months than go live without full guardrails. The article said 37% have already slowed down to build in safety guardrails. Serbinis wrote that healthcare has always met rising demand by adding people, but that model no longer works, and he described the infinite care team as a care team that never sleeps. He said a different vendor, tool and set of safeguards for every use case adds complexity and technical debt with each launch.

League is showing AI Front Door and AI Care Companion live at Booth #2836, alongside the Forge console, where attendees can watch completions, escalations and accuracy by use case in real time. People not going to HLTH can watch a live AI Care Companion webinar instead. League is a proud sponsor of Healthcare Scene. Serbinis holds a BSc in engineering physics from Queen’s University and an MSc in industrial engineering from the University of Toronto. The article leaves open what the solutions cost and which organizations have signed on.

Articles.Title: The Executive Guide to Scaling Agentic AI in Healthcare

stories.Headline: Why bond king Jeffrey Gundlach is steering clear of the AI 'blast radius'
stories.Summary:
Jeffrey Gundlach is avoiding artificial intelligence stocks during a period of sector decline. The DoubleLine founder spoke about his strategy at Yahoo Finance Invest on November 12, 2026. He is steering clear of what he calls the blast radius of the AI trade. This decision follows a market crash triggered by Election Day results. Gundlach has focused on this avoidance strategy since September.

The S&P 500 lost 4.4 percent and 3 trillion dollars on November 5. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,280 points, its worst single day since 2020. The Nasdaq fell 4.8 percent, affecting cloud and semiconductor firms like Sandisk and Micron. Gundlach now holds only 30 percent of his portfolio in equities. He recommends the equal-weighted S&P 500 and a barbell approach to bonds.

DoubleLine CEO Jeffrey Gundlach says he is avoiding cap-weighted index funds. He claims these funds have a concentration of about 60 percent in AI assets. Gundlach stated he rotated his investments after sensing a shift in the mania. He believes it is important to stay as diversified as possible. He intends to maintain this cautious investment position for a while.

Investors are worried that Democratic governors and senators elected on Election Day will hinder AI expansion. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has further damaged market sentiment. Huang allegedly had affairs with an Nvidia executive and a Chinese spy. Nvidia is considered the epicenter of the AI boom's financial commitments. Any disruption to the company is viewed as a negative for AI investors.

The AI sector has been crushed by the weight of its own high expectations. A blue wave of Democratic victories on Election Day sparked fears about the trade. This political shift led to a brutal trading session for many investors. Tech names have continued to trade with a downward bias recently. These factors combined to create a volatile environment for technology stocks.

Gundlach will continue to avoid the AI epicenter for the foreseeable future. He remains low in equities compared to his historical weighting. The articles do not state when the market might recover from the rout. They leave open whether Democratic officials will actually muck up AI expansion. It is unclear how Nvidia will replace its resigned chief executive.

Articles.Title: Why bond king Jeffrey Gundlach is steering clear of the AI 'blast radius'

stories.Headline: Frida Kahlo’s Image Has Become a Global Brand. A Viral AI-Generated Ad Makes Things Worse.
stories.Summary:
A viral AI-generated advertisement for the fashion brand Les Énervés, which has roots in Paris and Bali, has drawn sharp criticism for its portrayal of the Mexican painter Frida Kahlo. The ad was first posted to Instagram in October and began spreading widely on X this month. In it, a bubblegum-chewing Kahlo drives a bus through Paris carrying the Mona Lisa and Vincent van Gogh, with his ear replaced by a steel prosthetic. The depiction shows her downing several drinks before driving, though the real artist struggled with alcohol and drug addiction.

The brand says the ad was directed by its founder, Wakim Krari, and produced using what it calls "AI, and a lot of patience." Its website adds that the bus was recreated as a Renault TN, a model that might have been seen in Paris when Kahlo staged an exhibition there in 1939. Les Énervés presents the ad as a statement of reclamation, saying that a hundred years after her 1925 bus accident, Kahlo is the one driving. The soundtrack moves from an Édith Piaf song to Britney Spears's "Gimme More," and the brand's website hints that a new chapter with a new muse is coming soon. Responsibility for the content rests with the brand and its founder, who have framed it as a tribute.

The article's author says the ad disrespects the dead, and notes that a post with 46,000 likes made the same point. The piece also points to other AI-generated Kahlo content, including a video that recasts her as a Spice Girl and a chatbot that answers as her. The author argues that Kahlo carefully built her own self-image, including her unibrow, men's clothing, and Tehuana skirts, in ways that resisted the expectations placed on a 20th-century Mexican woman. The commercial spread of her image on items ranging from Barbie dolls to tequila bottles is described as already wearing down those nuances. Curator Mari Carmen Ramírez, of a Tate Modern show called "Frida: The Making of an Icon," has said her image has become subsumed by artists and activists.

The article also raises concern about how AI can distort art history, using the ad's sidelining of Diego Rivera as an example. Kahlo's 25-year relationship with Rivera was complicated, marked by love and frustration, and he betrayed her by having an affair with her younger sister. Kahlo died at 47 in 1954, when she was far less famous than she is today, so she cannot respond to the ad. The author concludes that the brand appears to have found its next target, and that its promised new chapter reads like a threat.

Articles.Title: Frida Kahlo’s Image Has Become a Global Brand. A Viral AI-Generated Ad Makes Things Worse.

stories.Headline: Anthropic CEO predicts AI could help cure major diseases within 10 years
stories.Summary:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in a 42-minute investor roadshow video released on November 10, 2026, that artificial intelligence could make diseases such as cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease and mental illness relics of the past within less than a decade. He also spoke of an "age of miracles" in which scientific advances could solve long-standing problems. His remarks came as Anthropic expands its work in biological research and drug development. The article's own coverage places them against a background of ongoing company activity and expert debate. In an October 27 company update, Anthropic said it had set up research partnerships with six organizations developing medicines and had started its own drug discovery programs.

Some of this work targets rare childhood diseases, including forms of muscular dystrophy. Anthropic acknowledged, however, that most of it remains preclinical, meaning the potential treatments have generally not reached human testing. The article presents this as the current state of the research rather than evidence of a finished medical result. Amodei's optimism echoes a view held by other technology leaders. Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis, speaking at the Indian Institute of Science, said developing a new drug typically takes about 10 years and suggested AI could cut that to months or even weeks.

He pointed to AlphaFold, which has generated predictions for more than 200 million protein structures, while acknowledging that predicting structures is only one part of making medicines. Researchers must still confirm that compounds work as intended, have suitable properties and avoid harmful side effects. The pharmaceutical industry has been more cautious. Jeff Leiden, executive chairman of Vertex Pharmaceuticals, told The Wall Street Journal that Vertex had evaluated about 50 AI companies using a database of 10,000 drug compounds, and none had independently produced a working drug. He rejected claims that AI could cure 90% of human diseases within seven years, calling them "complete BS."

The article notes that drugs must still pass laboratory research, preclinical studies, human clinical trials and regulatory review before they are proven safe and effective. The article concludes that AI may help researchers identify targets, analyze biological data and speed early-stage discovery, but that these abilities do not remove the scientific uncertainties of developing treatments. Amodei's prediction, it says, reflects the possibilities he sees rather than an established medical timeline. Whether such expectations become treatments for the world's most difficult diseases within a decade remains, in the article's words, an open question.

Articles.Title: Anthropic CEO predicts AI could help cure major diseases within 10 years

stories.Headline: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
stories.Summary:
A study by IP protection firm Podqi, shared exclusively with The Verge, found that AI chatbots recommended fake retail websites, and The Verge reported the findings on November 12, 2026. The study tested ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with shopping-related questions about 151 brands, including Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, Madhappy, and Le Creuset. Podqi crafted its own prompts, such as “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?” and “Where can I find [brand] online?” The test ran over two testing periods in September and used a tool that tracks AI answers across chatbots.

Over 6,795 answers, Podqi found that all three AI engines cited and showed shoppers risky sites. Podqi defined risky sites as fake websites impersonating real retailers or selling knockoffs, old brand domains reregistered by someone else, or dead sites someone else could purchase and reuse. Gemini showed risky sites least often, linking to or mentioning one in 4 percent of answers, while Perplexity performed worst at 15 percent and ChatGPT fell in the middle at 8 percent. ChatGPT offered warnings about each risky site it surfaced 24 percent of the time, the best of the three. Queries related to larger companies had risky sites in answers about half as often as smaller brands.

AI displayed risky sites more often when asked about regional brand websites, and the engines at times listed fake regional sites for brands that have none. Podqi CEO and cofounder Trevor West said part of the effort is making sure consumers know it is always best to verify the source before entering personal information or credit card information, even when a chatbot feeds them a result. Google spokesperson Jessica Levis Boord said the company takes information quality seriously and was happy Gemini performed best among the products tested. Boord said Google continually works to test and improve its models and is upfront that Gemini is AI and can make mistakes, so it displays links to sources alongside responses to help people verify information. OpenAI spokesperson Taya Christianson said the goal is for ChatGPT to connect people with reliable places to shop.

Christianson said OpenAI is continuing to improve its safeguards to make potentially deceptive sites less likely to appear in shopping-related results and appreciates researchers sharing examples. Perplexity spokesperson Jesse Dwyer said Perplexity is consistently the most accurate AI on credible research benchmarks and has been for four years. Dwyer said the company never claims to be 100 percent accurate but does claim to be the only company relentlessly focused on it. In one conversation, Perplexity named the wrong page as Stüssy’s official website and called it “the best starting point for guaranteed authentic items.” AI companies market chatbots as helpful for shopping tasks like researching, comparing, and discovering products or retailers, and the issue could be especially relevant going into the upcoming holiday shopping season.

It is likely that more consumers will be using AI to shop this year, including buying products from brands or sites they are not already familiar with. The study prompted the chatbots with a handful of shopping-related questions involving a selection of 151 brands. Questions included “Does [brand] ship internationally? What are their regional websites?”

The test asked about 151 small and large companies, including fashion brands Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, and Madhappy, a client of Podqi, and homeware brand Le Creuset. Mentions of risky sites include instances of recommending a risky site, displaying it without comment, and warning a user about it. AI citing fake sites is a headache for brands and retailers and could also quickly become a risk for consumers. The Verge published the story on November 12, 2026, at 5:00 PM UTC, written by features writer Mia Sato.

The article did not say whether Podqi plans to repeat the test or publish the full set of prompts and answers. It did not say whether the AI companies plan changes to how regional websites are handled in shopping answers. It did not say how many of the 6,795 answers came from each chatbot. It did not say whether any consumer reported losing money or personal information because of a risky site.

Articles.Title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds

stories.Headline: Hub: More streamers using AI to search for content
stories.Summary:
Hub Entertainment Research released new data on Thursday, November 12, 2026, showing that streaming viewers are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence chatbots and similar programs to find something to watch. According to the survey, two in five streamers now use tools such as ChatGPT and Google's AI Mode for recommendations and to search for particular shows and movies across different platforms. That share rises to 57 percent among streamers aged 16 to 34. The research was conducted in October and drew on responses from more than 1,600 U.S. consumers.

Among those already using AI for entertainment discovery, 57 percent said the technology works better than traditional search engines. Viewers in this group also feel that the built-in search and discovery tools on streaming platforms often fail to connect them with the content they want at a given moment. Personal recommendations still lead as the most common discovery method, with 29 percent of streamers finding a new favorite through word of mouth from family or friends and 21 percent crediting movie and TV trailers. Only 14 percent credited a streaming service's own algorithm. The data also found that younger viewers are finding older shows: nearly one in four streamers aged 16 to 24 said a classic TV series was their top new discovery over the past year, compared with 11 percent of viewers over 35.

Hub Entertainment Research Senior Consultant Jason Platt Zolov, in a statement, said viewers have plenty to watch and simply need better ways to find it. The articles place this finding within a broader push by connected TV platforms to add AI to their search and discovery features. Samsung announced in August 2025 that its smart TV home screen would get an AI-powered makeover aimed at more personalized recommendations, and earlier this year it said it was partnering with Nielsen's Gracenote metadata business to improve those recommendations. Google has incorporated Gemini into newer versions of its Android TV platform since last year, and LG, Roku and Apple have made similar moves. Amazon has long used its Alexa assistant on Fire TV devices to help viewers find content across its own platforms and some partner apps.

Articles.Title: Hub: More streamers using AI to search for content

stories.Headline: As Microsoft services return online, company says outage wasn't caused by AI or cyberattack
stories.Summary:
Microsoft services including Outlook, Teams and its Copilot AI tool went down starting Thursday, and the outage lasted more than 24 hours as of Friday morning, affecting millions of customers worldwide. Microsoft said the incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. The company said it had addressed the underlying issue and was continuing to restore service to remaining customers and regions. It is estimated the outage could have cost billions of dollars in lost productivity.

Microsoft said there was no indication the outage was the result of malicious or cyber activity, and it also said the disruption was not caused by artificial intelligence. The company's statements appeared to be an attempt to push back on rumors circulating online that linked the outage to Microsoft laying off experienced workers or increasingly relying on AI in its workflows. Despite the disruptions, many people took to social media to celebrate what became an impromptu work holiday. The outage was reported by KUOW, which covers artificial intelligence, tech and the local economy in the Pacific Northwest.

Microsoft, based in Redmond, Washington, is responsible for the services and issued the statements about the cause. The company said the incident came from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. It said it had addressed the underlying issue and was restoring service to remaining customers and regions. Microsoft also confirmed there was no indication of malicious or cyber activity.

The outage hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot starting Thursday and was still affecting customers more than 24 hours later on Friday morning. Microsoft said service was being restored to remaining customers and regions after the underlying issue was addressed. The company's update came as rumors spread online about the cause, including claims tied to layoffs and AI use. Many customers celebrated the forced break on social media.

Articles.Title: As Microsoft services return online, company says outage wasn't caused by AI or cyberattack

stories.Headline: AI Recording Devices: Competing to Be the "One That Understands You Best"
stories.Summary:
AI recording devices are competing to be the tool that understands users best through various hardware forms. Nooklab secured backing from HSG and Linear Capital in early 2026 while still in the idea stage. Flowtica raised tens of millions of RMB in October 2026 from Vertex, Source Code Capital, 5Y Capital and Qingshuiwan Fund. These companies are creating intelligent hardware for voice recording to capture personal context. The market is shifting from simple recording hardware toward the narrative of personal context agents.

Nooklab's Moonphase Flip weighs 54 grams and extracts schedules through non-intrusive recording. Flowtica's Verso weighs 78 grams and features a permanent e-ink screen for real-time transcription. Plaud Note is less than 3mm thick, weighs 30g, and is the size of a credit card. DingTalk A1 Pro has a 2980mAh battery for 180 hours of recording and 180 days of standby. Dreame uses alligator leather and 3.5mm real diamonds with an embedded NFC electronic business card.

Mo Zihao, the former CEO of Plaud China, prefers the term AI Work Companion over AI voice recorder. He views the hardware as a Trojan horse for customer acquisition to drive software subscriptions. Plaud reported that its software subscription ARP grew from 1 million USD to 100 million USD in two years. The company achieved a valuation of 2 billion RMB and a 25% profit margin per unit. Nearly 50% of Plaud hardware users upgraded to paid subscriptions before the brand entered China.

Users are affected by the shift toward hybrid work and long online meetings after the pandemic. An entrepreneur told Xiaguang She that BOM costs for 1000 RMB cards are actually under 100 RMB. This low cost has pushed the Chinese entry threshold down from 1000 RMB to 499 RMB. Tencent Research Institute found Chinese AI users typically pay between 30 and 100 RMB monthly. North American payment rates for AI products are 15% to 40%, while Chinese rates are 3% to 13%.

The market includes wearable options like the 10 gram Anker AI recording bean and Stream Ring. Memoket offers an 11 gram wristband, while Shokz and Mobvoi use open-ear or 4G earphone designs. iFlytek Magic uses a touch screen, and Flowtica Scribe integrates handwriting and shooting functions. Most devices use miniature capacitive MEMS microphones, which cost less than 10 RMB each. American consumers hold an average of 4.5 digital subscriptions with an average monthly spend of 84 USD.

Apple released developer betas for iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3 on November 4 with new AI functions. These features allow users to review the last 15 seconds of conversation and organize daily summaries. Domestic retail sales for online voice recorders reached 140 million RMB in the first quarter of 2026. Average prices rose from 334.8 RMB in January to 386.3 RMB in March. The articles leave open whether Chinese users will develop stable habits for paying software subscriptions.

Articles.Title: AI Recording Devices: Competing to Be the "One That Understands You Best" - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Pilot Tests Show Feasibility of AI Patient Simulations in Medical Training
stories.Summary:
Researchers at a United States medical school conducted a pilot study on AI patient simulations. The team tested these encounters with first-year medical students in November 2026. They wanted to see if large language models could be used for clinical training. The study compared two different ways of delivering the simulation. All participants completed the assigned tasks without any total technical failures.

The project involved 19 students recruited from a pool of 72, which was a 26 percent rate. Seven students were placed in a facilitated group, while 12 worked in a self-paced individual format. The group session lasted about 35 minutes, and the individual sessions had a median length of 31 minutes. Researchers used the Behavioral Safety Language Scale-Provisional to measure student perceptions. Most students, or 58 percent, preferred a hybrid model of working alone first and then in a group.

Shelley Tischkau, James Lynch, Sean McGinity, Andrew Primous, Elijah Meldrim, Samantha Lynch, and Richard Selinfreund led the investigation. They noted that the simulation was feasible and received favorable ratings from the students. However, the authors stated that the results are exploratory and do not prove educational effectiveness. They explained that the data must be confirmed with a larger, randomized sample. The team also mentioned that some students experienced intermittent technical problems.

This research fits into a broader effort to use generative AI for case-based and problem-based learning. Current medical education research often lacks specific details on delivery formats and outcome measurements. This pilot study attempted to fill those gaps by testing distinct learning environments. The researchers used Wilcoxon signed-rank exact tests and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to analyze the data. Future studies will be needed to determine if these tools actually improve medical training.

Articles.Title: Pilot Tests Show Feasibility of AI Patient Simulations in Medical Training

stories.Headline: "No path to real use": a veteran Microsoft AI scientist quits, says research that could halve AI costs wasn't even seriously considered
stories.Summary:
John Langford, a veteran researcher, left Microsoft in November 2026. He co-founded the AI Frontiers lab and worked there for over 14 years. His group of roughly 50 people was absorbed into Microsoft AI in September. Langford claims the company ignored research that could halve AI costs. He believes the current leadership only cares about scaling models.

Microsoft AI was formed in March 2024 by Mustafa Suleyman and Karén Simonyan. AI Frontiers was reorganized into this division in early September 2026. Langford previously joined the New York City lab in May 2012. He developed Vowpal Wabbit and served as ICML president from 2019 to 2021. His Full Bandwidth Transformer research was published in August.

Langford stated that Microsoft AI has a philosophy of scaling and aggressively not research. He said he was not comfortable at a company where his work had no path to use. He believes the deal to do good work for good results is broken. He described the current situation as a bit of a train wreck. He noted that his team was non-consensually reorganized.

An anonymous commenter moving into Microsoft AI expressed similar feelings to Langford. ByteDance's Seed team published Recycler on October 25, which uses similar methods. Langford says this proves his research could match models of twice the size. This affects an industry with investments approaching a trillion dollars. Microsoft is also offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees.

Langford created AI Frontiers in 2023 after the release of ChatGPT. The group developed the AutoGen framework and the Fara-7B computer use model. Microsoft Research previously produced Phi small language models for the Edge browser. Satya Nadella has discussed 20 million AI agents doing work. Microsoft is scaling back Copilot features in Windows 11.

AI Frontiers is over and will not offer internships next year. Microsoft's AI Frontiers page says the lab continues to pursue frontier research. The company is building a superintelligence lab announced at Build 2026. Langford believes Microsoft could become attractive for research if leaders develop more wisdom. The articles leave open if Microsoft will respond publicly.

Articles.Title: "No path to real use": a veteran Microsoft AI scientist quits, says research that could halve AI costs wasn't even seriously considered

stories.Headline: Microsoft says service is returning to normal, AI not to blame for ‘historic’ outage
stories.Summary:
Microsoft said its services were returning to normal after a global outage that disrupted work for millions of customers, and it said artificial intelligence was not to blame. The disruption began around midday Thursday and affected Outlook email, Teams messaging and the Copilot AI assistant. The company said the underlying issue was resolved and that the cause was a technical issue not related to cyber activity or AI. Microsoft said it saw broad recovery and stability across its services.

The outage hit government workers, hospital employees, business owners and students. Hospitals in the UK temporarily relied on paper records, according to the BBC, and pharmacies there were concerned about filling prescriptions. US congressional staffers told Politico that the outage derailed policy negotiations. Microsoft said it restored services gradually and validated stability at each stage, which took longer but helped ensure a stable restoration. The company promised a post mortem later.

Microsoft said initial information showed the outage was not the result of a malicious attack. Cybersecurity expert and former Microsoft employee Katie Moussouris told The Post that the global scale and the duration made the incident historic. She noted that Microsoft’s alert system appeared not to work and said something really bad must have happened for the cascade to last so long and for the company to be unable to recover. The company is a major partner with OpenAI and Anthropic, and both saw technical failures with their products during the outage, according to reports.

The disruption came during a challenging time for Microsoft, which recently offered buyouts to more than a quarter of its workforce, 60,000 employees, as it looked to cut costs and restructure staff for AI. Last year the company laid off 9,000 employees. Industry experts and users on social media conjectured that the cost cutting brought on the outage, though they offered no evidence. Microsoft has been doubling down on building AI infrastructure and securing partnerships with OpenAI and Anthropic.

Articles.Title: Microsoft says service is returning to normal, AI not to blame for ‘historic’ outage

stories.Headline: US officials: multiple US DOJ probes threaten to sweep up Nvidia, including one focused on antitrust grounds and two focused on Megaspeed and Supermicro (Rohan Goswami/Semafor)
stories.Summary:
Two administration officials told Semafor that multiple US Justice Department probes could sweep up Nvidia, as fallout from former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation continues to spread through Washington. One inquiry is an antitrust investigation focused specifically on the chipmaker, according to those officials. Two other probes center on the tech companies Megaspeed and Supermicro. The article was published on November 12, 2026.

The Megaspeed and Supermicro inquiries reportedly focus on the involvement of Alice Huang, whom the article describes as an alleged Chinese spy. The article says Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with her before he resigned. Nothing in the reporting indicates that the Justice Department intends to bring criminal charges against Nvidia or against Jensen Huang at this time. Semafor's account of the probes rests on the two officials, and the article does not describe any formal public filing or announcement by the department.

Nvidia and the Justice Department declined to comment to Semafor. Megaspeed and Supermicro did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The article does not say whether the probes have produced any findings, subpoenas, or next steps. Its details come entirely from officials speaking to the reporter, and the piece leaves open how the investigations will unfold.

Articles.Title: US officials: multiple US DOJ probes threaten to sweep up Nvidia, including one focused on antitrust grounds and two focused on Megaspeed and Supermicro (Rohan Goswami/Semafor)

stories.Headline: Struggling marijuana farms pivot to becoming AI data center sites to escape falling weed revenue
stories.Summary:
Struggling marijuana farms are pivoting to become AI data center sites to escape falling weed revenue, Tom's Hardware reported on 12 November 2026. The article said the AI data center boom is bringing hope to struggling cannabis farmers. Several growers are considering selling their cultivation facilities or converting them into "mini data center nodes," the article said. The article cited Arizona Public Media for the cannabis industry's decline. The article said sales peaked in 2024 and oversupply drove prices down.

The article said the facilities already have electricity and water infrastructure that is increasingly hard to get. It cited Forbes looking at a 32,850-square-foot cannabis facility in Kalamazoo, Michigan, wired for 1.5 megawatts. The article said that capacity can be expanded to 2.5 megawatts in under a year and 15 megawatts in the long term. The article said the facility is provisioned for fiber internet and equipped with a state-of-the-art HVAC system for climate control. The article said the concept is dubbed "adaptive reuse."

Moe Asnani, former owner of two Tucson D2 Dispensaries, told Arizona Public Media there is a lot more cannabis grown in Arizona than Arizonans use. Asnani said a lot of folks are getting out of that business, like himself, at least on the cultivation side. Asnani said the facilities can potentially be repurposed to be mini data center nodes. Asnani said the whole idea is to create smaller nodes where people control their own data and are not at the mercy of other people's updates. Asnani said he believes in decentralization.

Tucson City Council member Paul Cunningham said data centers are "dirty words" and everybody knows that. Cunningham said no one wants to build a brand-new data center anywhere. Cunningham said he is OK with exploring the option if buildings were already using that amount of water and energy in their previous function and it can be done without being invasive. Niki Krear, vice president of acquisitions of real estate investment trust New Lake Capital Partners, told MJBizDaily that operators look for a sweet spot between connectivity, costs, and regulation. Krear said it is a combination of finding affordable power, dense fiber networks, and favorable tax policies.

The article said cannabis farming is both power- and water-intensive. The article said data centers often demand twice to thrice more power than cultivation facilities, with upgrades possibly taking up to five years. The article said data center operators looking for smaller sites may have to contend with NIMBY fights from neighbors. The article said there may be zoning restrictions, moratoriums, and regulatory hurdles. The article said the lack of economies of scale could end up costing operators more.

The article said OpenAI and Anthropic are interested in small data centers as massive hyperscale sites face opposition from the community. The article said Cunningham called adaptive reuse a more palatable alternative to massive, purpose-built sites sitting on the outskirts of town. The article said there is massive demand for data centers but it is not a guaranteed payoff for struggling cash-strapped growers looking to unload their unprofitable properties. The article said increased competition, costs, and taxes face the farmers amid reduced demand for marijuana. The article did not say which growers are converting or when any conversion would happen.

Articles.Title: Struggling marijuana farms pivot to becoming AI data center sites to escape falling weed revenue

stories.Headline: Photon Joins SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network to Help Enterprises Put AI to Work
stories.Summary:
Photon Group, an enterprise AI consulting and engineering firm based in Dublin, has joined the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network, known as SpaceXSI, and has set out the focus of the collaboration as helping enterprises adopt AI across software engineering and business workflows. The announcement was published on November 12, 2026. Photon is a Launch Partner in the network, which was announced on October 22, 2026, and it takes part in the network's Transformation Partner program. Photon says it will bring consulting and engineering services that help clients find relevant use cases, redesign workflows and put SpaceXSI capabilities into existing systems. Its Forward Deployed Engineers will work inside client environments to support implementation and adoption.

For agent-based solutions, Photon will also offer PHTN.ai, its Enterprise Agent Management platform, which is built to orchestrate, govern and monitor AI agents. The partnership will concentrate on three areas: software engineering, where development teams adopt AI within their delivery processes, supported by training and workflow redesign; business workflow transformation, where industry-specific processes are targeted and AI capabilities are built into the systems employees already use; and agent deployment and oversight, where PHTN.ai supplies orchestration, human-review controls and visibility into agent actions. The platform is described as domain-aware and LLM-agnostic, meaning it works across different models, frameworks and cloud environments. Clients can set human-review requirements and monitor agent activity as deployments grow. Photon's Universal Agent Harness serves as the shared foundation for these functions.

Srinivas Balasubramanian, Photon's chief executive, said clients want to know where AI can improve their business and how to move it into production, and that Photon will handle the business problem, the engineering and the adoption work. Mukund Balasubramanian, the company's president and chief technology officer, said that building an AI workflow and running it reliably are linked responsibilities, and that PHTN.ai controls what agents can access, which actions they can take and when a person must review their work. Toni Adams, head of partnerships at SpaceX Super Intelligence, welcomed Photon to the network and said the two companies look forward to helping customers adopt AI across software development and business operations. Photon describes itself as serving 40% of the Fortune 100 across banking, financial services, retail, consumer goods, healthcare and automotive. The release provides no financial terms, timeline for specific client results, or details on how the partnership will be measured.

Articles.Title: Photon Joins SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network to Help Enterprises Put AI to Work

stories.Headline: AI1000: Bot Access and Blocking Reveal an AI Readiness Divide Ahead of Holiday 2026
stories.Summary:
Retailers were ranked on AI shopping readiness in a new benchmark released November 12, 2026, by ReFiBuy and Digital Commerce 360. The quarterly AI1000 index, which covers 1,000 leading online retailers in North America, combines AI traffic measures with bot-access and commerce-protocol signals. The Q3 edition reports an average score of 39.9 out of 100. Costco is the biggest climber, rising 182 places to No. 325, while GoPro and Scheels gained 173 and 168 places respectively.

The results point to a divide between retailers that welcome AI shopping agents and those that do not. Only 13 of the 100 largest online retailers rank in the AI1000 top 100, and all five leaders sit outside the top 100 by sales for the third straight edition. Nixon leads on AI readiness, followed by Online Labels, Everlane, CustomInk, and Brooklinen. Adoption of the Universal Commerce Protocol, which lets AI agents complete checkout for shoppers, also varies widely, with 55% of jewelry retailers showing endpoints compared with 3% of automotive parts and accessories retailers.

ReFiBuy CEO Scot Wingo said some major platforms, including Amazon and eBay, are deliberately blocking bots, and a larger group of retailers appear to be blocking them too. He said it is unclear whether those decisions were strategic or came from IT or infrastructure teams without input from commerce staff. Wingo warned that such blocking will significantly reduce discovery traffic for holiday 2026. The release advises commerce and security teams to set separate permissions for search crawlers, model-training crawlers, and shopping agents, and to test whether approved agents can retrieve useful product data.

The release also recommends that retailers maintain accurate, consistent product data, including current availability and delivery terms for holiday shoppers, ahead of planning for 2027. ReFiBuy offers an ACO audit to identify catalog gaps and monitoring to track how agents discover products after updates. Retailers in the index can view their personalized Q3 report at refibuy.ai/ai1000 after verifying a work email. The company describes itself as the inventor of Agentic Commerce Optimization, a term it uses to frame this work.

Articles.Title: AI1000: Bot Access and Blocking Reveal an AI Readiness Divide Ahead of Holiday 2026

stories.Headline: NRG Launches AI Observatory, a Monthly Tracker of Everyday AI Use Among US Adults
stories.Summary:
National Research Group, a company owned by Stagwell (NASDAQ: STGW), launched AI Observatory on November 12, 2026, a monthly tracker of how artificial intelligence fits into everyday life for American adults. Each month the program surveys roughly 1,000 US adults ages 18 to 64, weighted to match national demographics, about their AI use, their feelings toward it, and their understanding of the technology. A parallel survey of roughly 100 AI Trailblazers, drawn from NRG's proprietary panel of AI superusers, adds the views of people who are further ahead in adopting it. The company says many AI polls focus on abstract social and political concerns or on how often people use the tools, and that both can miss the lived experience.

NRG built the program to close that gap, noting that many people express concern about AI's effect on jobs and society yet tend to feel positive once they use it. The program's central measure is the AI Proximity Score, a single number from 0 to 100 showing how integrated AI has become in a person's life. It averages four equally weighted components, each scored 0 to 100: AI Use, which covers how often people use AI; AI Reach, which covers the areas of life AI touches, such as work, school, home, entertainment, and hobbies; AI Roles, which covers the tasks people give AI across tool, assistant, and teammate roles; and AI in Conversation, which covers how often people discuss AI with others. In the latest survey, the national score was 42 out of 100, which NRG says points to broad adoption that has not yet become fully integrated into daily life.

The company reports that proximity tracks closely with attitudes: 86% of high-proximity adults say AI will have a positive impact on society, compared with 53% of moderate-proximity and 27% of low-proximity adults. High-proximity users also feel more secure about their jobs, at 68% compared with 45% of moderate-proximity users. The program also tracks which AI companies are rising or falling, measuring momentum as the share saying a company is rising minus the share saying it is falling. David Byler, Vice President at National Research Group, said he spent years studying the social, demographic, and cultural currents that shape public opinion, and described AI as having moved from fiction to one of the core forces shaping American life.

Rob Barrish, Head of Technology Strategy at the company, said AI is becoming part of people's daily routines while businesses make decisions about products and customer relationships without a clear picture of what people value or trust. Barrish argued that the research gives leaders evidence while they can still shape how people adopt AI. The articles say the program is meant as a reference for businesses, policymakers, journalists, and researchers, and that it is designed to understand people and society rather than to advocate for or against AI. Five months of data are already available, with the next wave being collected now and new findings to be added monthly.

Articles.Title: NRG Launches AI Observatory, a Monthly Tracker of How AI Shows Up in the Daily Lives of American Adults

stories.Headline: Red Hat joins race to be ‘air traffic controller’ for AI agents
stories.Summary:
Red Hat announced general availability of its agentic AI management tools for OpenShift 5 at the KubeCon conference in Salt Lake City this week. The release includes an MCP server and an MCP gateway, while MCP support for RHEL and Developer Hub is coming soon. Managing AI agents has become a top enterprise concern as models grow more capable, and uncontrolled agents can cause significant harm. Red Hat is now positioning itself as one of the options for a central control plane.

The MCP gateway sits between AI agents and the tools they call, filtering what each agent can see based on its credentials. It includes NeMo Guardrails, an open source toolkit from Nvidia, which can block prompt injections and protect sensitive data. The gateway can also require human approval for agent actions that change systems. The new OpenShift MCP server ties agent access to existing identity systems and Kubernetes role-based permissions, with audit trails for agent activity. An agent sandbox in technology preview can isolate untrusted agent code in virtual machines.

Red Hat is also promoting OpenShift LightSpeed from a conversational chatbot to an AI agent that can diagnose cluster problems, propose fixes, and assess the risk of updates. In technology preview, it can take on more troubleshooting tasks, with a human approving every change. OpenShift 5 adds hardened multi-tenancy for sovereign deployments and expands support for post-quantum cryptography. Red Hat is also offering a free year of OpenShift Virtualization for qualifying three-year agreements.

Red Hat's head of product for developer tools, Balaji Sivasubramanian, said Red Hat Developer Hub 2.1 gives developers and AI agents governed access to enterprise context. The Developer Hub 2.1 MCP server is expected to be generally available later this month. Red Hat also said an MCP server for RHEL is coming in the coming weeks, letting enterprises use agents to diagnose RHEL issues without unrestricted access. Analysts say the release matters for Red Hat customers, since OpenShift 4 came out in 2019. Dell'Oro analyst Mauricio Sanchez said enterprises with heavy server and software investments should shortlist Red Hat.

Analysts say Red Hat's advantage is that its platform runs across cloud and on-premises and works with AI systems from many providers, which helps avoid vendor lock-in. Leapwork's Donovan Brady said Microsoft's Azure Agent 365 is stronger, because it supports agents wherever they are deployed and Red Hat lacks that single control plane. Sanchez said Red Hat's capabilities lag some rivals and its oversight of agents on other platforms is limited. Brady said OpenShift Virtualization is technically viable as a VMware alternative, but switching requires rearchitecting the data center. ABI Research's Dimitris Mavrakis said the one-year free license is not the strongest reason to migrate.

Sanchez said the race for agent management has not been decided and is only in its early stages. IDC analyst Jim Mercer said OpenShift is increasingly competing in virtualization, AI infrastructure, agentic operations and enterprise security. Matt Kimball of Moor Insights & Strategy said Red Hat's approach gives agents governed access and keeps a human in the loop. The articles do not say whether Red Hat can take on more agentic AI management, and they do not say how the MCP server for RHEL or Developer Hub 2.1 will perform after release.

Articles.Title: Red Hat joins race to be ‘air traffic controller’ for AI agents

stories.Headline: Microsoft vs. Meta: enterprise AI distribution against monetization speed
stories.Summary:
Microsoft Corporation and Meta Platforms Inc are competing for dominance in the artificial intelligence sector as of November 13, 2026. Microsoft is focusing on enterprise distribution, while Meta is prioritizing the speed of monetization. Both companies have invested heavily in infrastructure to secure their positions. This competition highlights a struggle between building a broad business ecosystem and achieving immediate financial returns.

Microsoft reported FY2026 revenue of $331.84B with 17.8% growth, while Meta reported FY2025 revenue of $200.97B with 22.2% growth. Both firms spent roughly 35% of their revenue on capital expenditures, specifically 34.9% for Microsoft and 34.7% for Meta. As of September 30, 2026, Microsoft had a P/E of 27.2x and Meta had a P/E of 21.5x. Microsoft's annualized AI revenue exceeded $37B by June 2026, and it generated $66.99B in levered free cash flow by June 30, 2026.

Analysts suggest that Microsoft leads in distribution through Azure, GitHub, and Copilot, but must prove its massive spending can create profitable workloads. Meta is seen as leading in efficiency because it applies AI directly to content ranking and advertising. Meta's revenue reached $64.60B as of October 21, 2026, though its shares dropped 6.54% following that release. Experts note that the market is now demanding clear proof of returns from both tech giants.

The current landscape is a race between distribution and monetization speed rather than a battle of specific models. Microsoft offers more options for enterprises, but Meta converts AI improvements into advertising revenue more quickly. Investors remain tense as they weigh these different strategies. The market will continue to penalize uncertain payback periods while rewarding clear financial returns.

Articles.Title: Microsoft vs. Meta: enterprise AI distribution against monetization speed

stories.Headline: Meta left AI videos of athlete abuse up after user reports — until journalists stepped in
stories.Summary:
Meta failed to remove AI-generated videos showing the abuse of young female athletes until journalists intervened. Reporter Maggie Harrison Dupré and her team at Futurism discovered the content during an investigation. They used a personal Facebook account to flag the material for review. The company initially ignored these reports and kept the accounts active.

The team flagged 10 pages that showed older male coaches inappropriately touching athletes who appeared to be teenagers.
