The project began 3.5 years earlier and has grown into a platform for running multi-modal large language models on hardware ranging from consumer machines to enterprise servers. It uses quantization, optimized backends and a portable C and C++ implementation to make inference widely accessible. Many downstream applications already depend on the project's work.

The release marks a commitment to developers who rely on the library interfaces. From now on, both llama.cpp and ggml will signal API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps, and the team said it will be stricter about making those boundaries visible to downstream consumers. The project currently supports more than 150 architecture variants and all mainstream speculative decoding methods. Its ggml engine runs on virtually any hardware through dedicated backends, each of which can be compiled as a dynamic library and optionally loaded at runtime.

The team said a flexible but stable API is paramount as local AI and privacy become more important. It credited an open-source community of highly skilled contributors and said maintaining a high quality codebase, staying in control of the architecture and understanding implementation details will remain top priorities. The team also said it is investing more resources in CI infrastructure, using Hugging Face technologies such as HF Buckets and HF Jobs to scale capacity and check every change landing on the master branches. It thanked hardware partners NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel for support in enrolling self-hosted runners across major platforms.

The post described the release as a significant milestone that would not have been possible without joint efforts, and it thanked long-time maintainers and all contributors. It said the team looks forward to expanding how ggml-org software is distributed and reaches developers and end-users, and pointed readers to a discussion on adding the projects to packaging and release pipelines. It also noted that the team continues to adapt and integrate LLMs into its development cycle in a thoughtful and reasonable manner. The post mentioned Llama desktop apps for MacOS and Windows, shipped by the team behind llama.cpp and Hugging Face.

Articles.Title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem

stories.Headline: Copper prices slid to near four-month low amid fears of hike in U.S. interest rates, lower demand, especially from AI
stories.Summary:
Global benchmark copper prices dropped to a nearly four-month low on Friday, November 13, 2026. This decline was driven by expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will increase interest rates. Lower industrial demand from China and the global technology sector also contributed to the slide. Investors also engaged in profit booking following a previous price rally.

The metal was trading at $13,461.99 per tonne, which is about 1.8% lower than the previous day. This shift follows mid-term elections in the United States that resulted in a divided government. Such a political outcome reduced fears regarding tariffs on refined copper imports. However, a fallout involving Nvidia created new worries about future investments in artificial intelligence.

The Federation of Indian Mineral Industries, known as FIMI, attributed the fall to a stronger U.S. dollar and weak industrial demand. FIMI stated that higher interest rates could increase the cost of the dollar-denominated metal. They noted that while short-term prices will be volatile, the long-term outlook is positive. This optimism is based on the growth of electric vehicles, renewable energy, and power infrastructure.

FIMI suggested that India must encourage domestic mining and processing to improve supply security. They argued that reducing import dependence is essential for the country. While lower prices help consumers by cutting costs, FIMI warned that a long decline might hurt exploration investments. The industry body believes that global mine supply constraints will eventually support prices.

Articles.Title: Copper prices slid to near four-month low amid fears of hike in U.S. interest rates, lower demand, especially from AI

stories.Headline: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
stories.Summary:
Researchers released XYBench on November 13, 2026, to test how AI assistants handle misguided user questions. This benchmark evaluates if models can identify misconceptions when users ask for help with the wrong approach. The project was developed by researchers at Allen Institute for AI, Carnegie Mellon, NVIDIA, and Johns Hopkins. It focuses on the XY problem, where a person asks for help with a mistaken solution. XYBench won the Best Resource Paper Award at the EMNLP 2026 conference.

The benchmark uses 8,115 real-world questions about programming, cooking, and home repair to measure model performance. It includes 1,557 questions from Stack Overflow, 184 from Stack Exchange, 102 curated examples, and 6,272 from WikiHow. The system tests Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-9B, and DeepSeek-V4 Pro. It measures pragmatic solution, pragmatic emphasis, and misconception identification to see if models prioritize the actual goal. Claude Sonnet 4.5 serves as the automated judge for these specific evaluations.

The developers stated that useful AI assistants must help users who ask misguided questions based on misconceptions. They explained that LLMs have a critical gap in recognizing implicit misconceptions and redirecting users toward effective solutions. The team hopes this tool helps researchers measure if model improvements make assistants better at recognizing mistaken assumptions. They noted that models often suggest solutions to the stated request while ignoring the underlying goal. The researchers believe models must act on inferred intent when it diverges from the literal request.

The evaluated models were less likely than humans to steer users away from mistaken approaches toward actual goals. On Stack Overflow, models focused on the underlying goal in only 35 to 41 percent of responses. In contrast, they focused on the stated request in 47 to 57 percent of their answers. An experiment including GPT-4.1 showed models are better at recognizing useful advice than producing it themselves. This gap affects users who lack the knowledge to ask the right questions to solve their problems.

The benchmark draws on pragmatics, a branch of linguistics concerning how context and intent shape meaning. To create the WikiHow questions, researchers used Sonnet 4.5 to generate plausible misconceptions in procedural guides. Human reviewers validated the automated judge by assessing 500 responses with agreement rates between 74.2 and 100 percent. An oracle experiment showed that providing the intended request increased solution rates but decreased misconception identification. The dataset was filtered to remove cases where answering the literal request was sufficient.

Researchers can now use XYBench to test if changes to prompting or training improve how models identify misconceptions. Future work may investigate which training methods help models act on what users need rather than literal requests. The current benchmark only covers procedural problems and queries written in the English language. Extending the tool to other languages, cultures, and conversational settings remains an open direction for research. The project aims to build models that offer useful advice despite a user's mistaken assumptions.

Articles.Title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question

stories.Headline: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
stories.Summary:
On November 13, 2026, Dillon Bailey, Pomi Lee and Rishabh Chadha published a walkthrough on huggingface.co showing a beverage can pick-and-place task. The task uses the UR17G arm, the Robotiq 2F-140 gripper and a beverage can composed in Isaac Sim. The authors check the assets' behavior and run a pick-and-place example with agent-generated controls. The example uses GPT-6 Sol, a frontier AI model, to help create and run the task code in an open Isaac Sim scene. The walkthrough was published as a Hugging Face article and received 6 upvotes.

The example requires Isaac Sim 6.2, the version used for the walkthrough, and its system requirements must be checked. SimReady Central, an open asset library on Hugging Face, supplies the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper and beverage can packages. The arm validation report uses the Robot-Body 4.0.0 profile and the gripper report uses Robot-Gripper 3.0.0, both recording passing PhysX driven-joint checks. An example gripper path is ~/ASSETS/hf/src/simready-assets-c7fa7615/Robotiq_2F_140/simready_usd/Robotiq_2F_140.usda. The task grasps the can, lifts it, moves it to a target and releases it, with a horizontal grasp using a 2 N·m drive-effort cap chosen through simulation tests.

The authors say SimReady means an OpenUSD asset has been prepared with properties needed for a defined simulation use case, such as collisions, mass, joints and joint drives. They say SimReady Foundation defines what features the asset needs, connecting profile, features and requirements. They say a robot can look visually correct while stationary but move or interact incorrectly when the simulation runs. They say asset structures vary, so the settings in the loaded scene are the starting point. They say the results apply to this scripted setup and do not establish robustness to uncertain object positions, different payloads or real hardware.

The walkthrough says SimReady Central lets you reuse robot and object assets with authored simulation properties and profile-validation evidence. It says the agent uses the isaac-sim-remote and usd-articulation skills to assemble the robot and validate its physics. It says the full task uses the isaac-sim-remote, manipulaition-ik and physics-simulation skills. It says the fixed setup has the can at a known position, an anchored robot and a clear, flat workspace, with no vision used and limited collision checks. It says deformation and liquid motion are not modeled, so the example does not test crushing.

The walkthrough says the 2 N·m drive-effort cap was not calibrated to fingertip forces or recommended by the manufacturer, and points to the Robotiq product sheet for hardware gripping-force specifications. It says contact and friction hold the can as the arm follows fixed waypoints without replanning. It says the controller coordinates the UR17G arm's movement with the Robotiq 2F-140 gripper's opening and closing. It says the sequence is approach, grasp, lift, hold, transfer and release, shown at 4× speed from a yellow pickup marker to a green target. It says the scene should be reset to the same starting state before retrying.

The walkthrough says SimReady Central is an open asset library on Hugging Face and refers readers to its announcement blog. It says the Robot Assembler tutorial covers manual assembly and the Adding a Manipulator Robot tutorial explains the controller. It says the 5 Steps to Create SimReady Assets for Robotics guide prepares your own robotics assets and the SimReady Central submission guide makes assets available to other developers. It cites Michael Wagner's voice-controlled VR demo and Maziyar Panahi's Microduck simulation as inspiration. It lists the Robotiq-Official/simready-assets, TeradyneRobotics/UniversalRobots and nvidia/simready-assets datasets and the SimReady Central Space.

The walkthrough says readers can browse SimReady Central, review profiles and requirements in SimReady Foundation alongside validation reports, and follow the Isaac Sim installation guide. It says readers can follow the Isaac Sim Agent Skills documentation to make bundled skills available to their agent. It says generated code and results can vary and the generated code should be inspected before adapting the task. It says readers should share their scene and results in the Hugging Face comments, including the assets and Isaac Sim version used. It leaves open how the approach performs beyond this scripted setup.

Articles.Title: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets

stories.Headline: Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI
stories.Summary:
Shield, an IT services provider, announced on November 13, 2026 that its Forge platform now uses OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to let AI agents navigate legacy portals that technicians previously had to log into and finish by hand. The work is assigned by Forge's AI Engineer to a computer-use agent, and technicians decide which actions it can take on its own and where they need to review or approve. Shield says these browser workflows are live, with thousands of runs each month across its IT providers. Phone calls, on-site work and remote-desktop tasks still need human involvement.

Shield says GPT-6 Astra was 35-40% faster on average than the legacy models it had used for computer-use tasks. The company reports faster execution, fewer failures and fewer timeouts, and says its teams spend less time writing detailed instructions to an agent or helping it through a task. Jain also says customer satisfaction is higher on tickets where AI is used, with speed of resolution being a critical factor. Shield is testing remote-desktop workflows that would let agents perform more complex actions directly on a computer's desktop.

Mayank Jain, Head of Technology at Shield, said the only time a human technician should be needed is for their judgment, not because work is blocked on access. He said that before GPT-6 Astra, Forge's agents could get stuck at systems they could not access, and customers had to wait for a technician to complete that step. Shield tried computer use with earlier models, but Jain said they were not reliable or fast enough. He said GPT-6 Astra was natural with computer use, and that watching it feels like watching a human click around.

Jain said many portals that manage tickets, devices and software licenses lack APIs, so an agent needs to navigate the screen much as a person would. He said a system without an API is usually an old-school system that is hard to use, even by a human. He said GPT-6 Astra lets Shield's agents log into portals and legacy websites and perform tasks that only a human could six months ago. Jain said that with GPT-6 Astra, Forge is now truly an extension of Shield's human technicians.

Articles.Title: Shield helps technicians hand off legacy portal work with OpenAI

stories.Headline: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
stories.Summary:
Cisco Talos is tracking the growing usage of AI enabled penetration testing frameworks. These tools automate reconnaissance and vulnerability testing to accelerate intrusions. The framework called ARTEX was published on GitHub in July 2026. It was developed under the pseudonym Autumn 27 for authorized security testing. Criminals and targeted intrusion campaigns began using it within weeks of release.

ARTEX uses a planner agent to break objectives into tasks for worker agents. It records findings in a shared graph and requires little operator input. The framework supports different large language models and the Model Context Protocol. Operators have deployed it alongside VShell, GoPhish, and AdaptixC2 on various infrastructures. Other frameworks include Hephaestus, PentAGI, and HexStrike AI which integrates with Claude Code.

Cisco Talos stated these frameworks are the new reality for modern attackers. They noted that AI can be a force multiplier for defenders too. Talos observed that ARTEX compresses work that previously took skilled teams days. They warned that these tools work at speeds impossible for humans to disrupt. The company emphasized that battle tested incident response plans are now imperative.

VAPOR PANDA targeted over 200 organizations in 14 countries starting October 17, 2026. Storm 0940 targeted 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants after compromising ConnectWise application credentials. Storm 3358 targeted financial organizations in Southeast Asia and is based in Cambodia. Unidentified actors targeted South Korean financial firms and stole code signing certificates. Other victims include government, defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, and telecommunications organizations.

These frameworks use open source tools like nmap and nuclei for automation. They leverage services such as Shodan, Censys, and residential proxies for mapping. Some tools use Telegram for control while others use web interfaces. The Volta Infostealer previously showed the precursor to autonomous victim prioritization. Attackers use these tools to find exposed credentials in public GitHub repositories.

Future evolutions will likely include autonomous lateral movement and data exfiltration. Attack chains may culminate in autonomous ransomware activation and data theft. One attacker generated 80,000 requests in 90 minutes using an authorization flaw. The articles leave open whether the complete framework was used in South Korea. They do not specify which specific LLMs are most effective for ARTEX.

Articles.Title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms

stories.Headline: Nvidia board says it is "in the process of selecting a search firm" for the CEO role and it has "not formally engaged any potential candidates" (CNBC)
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced on Thursday, November 13, 2026, that CEO Jensen Huang would step down from his position. This decision followed reports of several affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The company board is now looking for a permanent replacement for the former leader. They have named CFO Colette Kress as the interim CEO to manage operations. Kress held her first executive meeting in Santa Clara on Thursday afternoon.

The board is currently choosing a search firm to help identify a new leader. They stated that they have not formally contacted any potential candidates yet. The company will consider both internal and external applicants for the role. This process follows reports that the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas. Haas previously worked at Nvidia for seven years before joining Arm in 2013.

The board of directors is responsible for the search and issued a statement to CNBC. They claimed that any speculation about specific candidates is premature at this time. The company also hired Wachtell Lipton on Tuesday to investigate foreign intelligence allegations. These probes involve Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, who is suspected of working for China. The board is managing these legal and leadership transitions simultaneously.

The news caused Nvidia shares to drop over 2 percent on Friday. This decline pushed the company's market cap below $4 trillion. Three House committees and the Senate Banking Committee want Huang to testify about national security. They are concerned that AI chips may have ended up in China. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also been asked to testify regarding these issues.

Articles.Title: Nvidia board says it is "in the process of selecting a search firm" for the CEO role and it has "not formally engaged any potential candidates" (CNBC)

stories.Headline: Microsoft apologizes for the outage, calling it a "technical issue" from a "network capacity upgrade", and says it was "not related to cyber or AI/agents" (@microsoft)
stories.Summary:
Microsoft apologized for a major outage in a post on X at 4:40 PM on November 13, 2026. The company said the disruption affected its customers and partners. Microsoft described the incident as a technical issue that was not related to cyber or AI/agents. The post drew 11.8 million views. Microsoft said the incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.

The company said it has addressed the underlying issue and is still restoring service to remaining customers and regions. Because of the scale of demand, Microsoft restored services gradually and validated stability at each stage. It said this took longer but helped ensure a stable restoration. Microsoft said it is deeply sorry for the disruption and knows the trust customers and partners place in its services.

It said it takes that responsibility extremely seriously. The company said it is seeing broad recovery and stability across its services. Microsoft said it will provide a full post-incident report once its review is complete. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Microsoft apologizes for the outage, calling it a "technical issue" from a "network capacity upgrade", and says it was "not related to cyber or AI/agents" (@microsoft)

stories.Headline: How Nvidia used a "scorched earth, adversarial attitude" targeting proponents of export controls in DC, invoking Trump's name to get license approvals expedited (Semafor)
stories.Summary:
In January, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter told government officials that Donald Trump and Jensen Huang wanted export license approvals expedited. Teter claimed he was with the president when the two men discussed the matter and insisted the process go fast. Nvidia used an adversarial attitude to target proponents of export controls and critics of the company in Washington. The chipmaker wielded an unprecedented level of influence to shape guidelines with global security and business implications for the industry. Teter regularly invoked the name of President Trump to push the agenda of the company through the government.

Nvidia objected to proposed license conditions for H200 chips to China, calling the cloud-customer requirement a poison pill. The company wanted know-your-customer checks to apply only to buyers purchasing tens of thousands of chips, worth billions of dollars. Teter pushed for end-of-life conditions to apply only to chips facing export controls in the United States. Nvidia told staffers that a location verification provision in the 2025 Chip Security Act was not technically feasible. The company later launched a location verification technology feature in May after demonstrating it privately for several months.

Tim Teter and Jensen Huang are described by a former official as having a scorched earth, adversarial attitude. Teter accused officials of misrepresenting products and policies, insisting that they carry out the agenda of President Trump. A Bureau of Industry and Security spokesperson said it is routine for agencies to work with individual companies. This spokesperson stated that Nvidia went through the same process as any other license applicant with non-political experts. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told the All-In podcast that he would help Huang have easy access to the president.

Congressional staffers said Nvidia used gaslighting and capitalized on a lack of technical expertise to water down various bills. Former staffers claimed the company lied about cyber vulnerabilities to argue against the 2025 Chip Security Act. Bloomberg reported that Nvidia undercounted Megaspeed sales to the government by 50,000 chips, which are worth billions of dollars. The Information reported that companies tied to suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang bought at least 7.5 billion dollars in chips. A former State Department official said they weighed blacklisting Megaspeed as early as the spring of 2025.

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia and served as CEO until he stepped down following reports of affairs with subordinates and a customer. The customer is suspected of being a Chinese spy, and the company became the world's most valuable firm. Huang developed a close relationship with Donald Trump, who viewed the company as crucial to his economic aspirations. Former AI czar David Sacks and Howard Lutnick were also key allies for the company in Washington. The company's GPUs sparked the modern AI era, and the US holds a nine-to-one compute advantage over China.

The departure of Jensen Huang has shaved 1.5 trillion dollars off the market value of the company. Many people in Washington are relishing the downfall of the former CEO after his aggressive lobbying tactics. The company declined to comment on the location-verification technology or the reports regarding its Washington influence. It remains unclear who started leaking news regarding the affair between Huang and the suspected Chinese spy. The relationship between Nvidia and government officials may become a defining scandal of the current presidency.

Articles.Title: How Nvidia used a "scorched earth, adversarial attitude" targeting proponents of export controls in DC, invoking Trump's name to get license approvals expedited (Semafor)
